sections.title: Advanced Production Integration
sections.en: 2.3 Advanced Production Integration As shown in Figure 2.55, in an advanced production integration system, SAP EWM controls all essential steps including component supply, supply of semi- finished materials, and receipt of finished or semi-finished products. There is no need for a delivery document on the ERP side. Advanced production supply using PMRs has several features including: The introduction of the new PMR object, which offers greater flexibility in the staging process within SAP EWM. A new option for SAP EWM staging has been added to the control cycle in addition to the existing pick parts and release order part options. The system supports single-order staging, cross-order staging, and manual staging. Status and quantity updates for manufacturing orders are supported. The system allows for user-driven staging via desktop transactions or in the background. Figure 2.55 Advanced Production Integration The advantages of using an advanced production integration system include the following: Once PMRs are created, your warehouse operations teams can work independently of SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The system allows for the warehouse to stage the quantity of components into smaller quantities (pallet by pallet staging), which provides flexibility in Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 96 better utilizing space in the production supply area or when manufacturing orders run over longer periods. Users have more flexibility to post goods issues for a material than was planned in PMR. PMR-based production supply uses a lean system communication approach by sending just one goods movement message to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, rather than creating several delivery documents. Advanced production integration provides flexibility to receive packed HUs from production lines or conveyor systems using radio frequency (RF) devices. The system also offers the option to return to the warehouse unused pallets that are no longer needed for production or any additional pallets sitting at a production supply area. SAP EWM is responsible for staging, adding more flexibility to augment production supply. In this section, we’ll walk through each part of advanced production integration, including staging, consumption, goods receipt, and clearing the production supply area bin for manufacturing orders as well as how to create part replenishments.

sections.title: Staging for Manufacturing Orders
sections.en: 2.3.1 Staging for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll delve into staging for manufacturing orders in advanced production integration processes, which involves the preparation and gathering of materials required for production. This phase includes activities such as creating PMRs from the warehouse and transferring them to the production area. Staging ensures that all necessary components are available when needed, thus optimizing the production process and minimizing delays. Business Process Business warehouses utilize a staging process to supply materials, whether packed or unpacked, to production and then consume these materials during the production process. To ensure that materials are supplied as needed and to prevent delays, the staging process is planned systematically with the help of advanced production integration in SAP EWM. When staging requires a large © 97 quantity or a significant amount of manufacturing time, production can occur either with the full requested quantity or with partial quantities, HU after HU. This approach also maximizes the utilization of space in the production supply area. As shown in Figure 2.56, with advanced production integration, the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system automatically creates a PMR in SAP EWM when a manufacturing order is released. This PMR triggers the warehouse management material staging process, which can be done manually or automatically. Figure 2.56 Material Staging for Production In SAP EWM, the Transaction /SCWM/STAGE (Schedule Staging for Production) can be used to create a staging warehouse task. This transaction can be executed manually or as a background job with input parameters such as warehouse, production staging area, and staging method. If a user needs to select a specific PMR and stage materials accordingly, the Web Dynpro user interface (UI) Transaction NWBC can be used to provide more flexibility and enable a user to view the stock overview in the production supply area. In advanced production integration, SAP EWM provides several options for staging materials, including the following: Single-order staging In this staging approach, the system generates a warehouse task for each line item in a PMR to move the product to the production supply area, as shown in Figure 2.57. Each warehouse task is linked to a single PMR, and once confirmed, the task is associated with the specific PMR item. The material and batch consumption posting can be done for the same PMR. If a HU or material Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 98 is not required for production, the user can manually release the PMR item reference for stock. The single-order staging method enables the staging of products for a particular PMR or for a PMR with unique characteristics. For example, products can be staged from a specific batch for a particular PMR. Figure 2.57 Single-Order Staging Cross-order staging In this material staging method, the system accumulates material from multiple PMRs and generates a warehouse task to move the material together. The warehouse task created in this method is not linked to any specific PMR item. After the warehouse task is confirmed, it does not have any reference to a PMR item. Consumption posting for material and batch can be posted for the PMR that has an item for the material and batch. This method offers flexibility since warehouse users can stage products for a single PMR or for several PMRs. To maintain a minimum quantity of the product on the production supply area, the bin assignment is used. If the sum of the quantity in the production supply area and open warehouse task quantity is less than the minimum quantity, the system generates a warehouse task to move the replenishment quantity to the production supply area. The replenishment quantity is also maintained in the bin assignment. In addition to single-order staging and cross-order staging, you also have the option for part replenishment creation or to use no order staging at all, but these methods are not as widely used so they will not be covered in depth here. sections.he:
‏Staging להזמנות ב-advanced production integration: הכנה ואיסוף החומרים הנדרשים לייצור, כולל יצירת PMRs מהמחסן והעברתם לאזור הייצור.

**תהליך עסקי** (Figure 2.56): מערכת SAP ERP/S4HANA יוצרת אוטומטית PMR ב-SAP EWM כשה-manufacturing order משוחררת. ה-PMR מפעיל את תהליך ה-material staging (ידני או אוטומטי). כש-staging דורש כמות גדולה או זמן ייצור רב, ניתן לייצר עם הכמות המלאה או בחלקים, HU אחר HU.

‏Transaction /SCWM/STAGE (Schedule Staging for Production) יוצרת staging warehouse task — ידנית או כ-background job עם פרמטרים (warehouse, ‏production staging area, ‏staging method). ל-flexibility ולצפייה ב-stock overview, ניתן להשתמש ב-Web Dynpro UI דרך NWBC.

אפשרויות staging:
• **Single-order staging** (Figure 2.57) — warehouse task לכל line item ב-PMR. כל task מקושר ל-PMR יחיד; לאחר אישור משויך ל-PMR item הספציפי. מאפשר staging מ-batch ספציפי ל-PMR מסוים.
• **Cross-order staging** — המערכת צוברת חומר מ-PMRs מרובים ויוצרת warehouse task משותף, שאינו מקושר ל-PMR item ספציפי. לשמירת כמות מינימום ב-PSA משמש ה-bin assignment: אם הסכום (כמות ב-PSA + open warehouse task) קטן מהמינימום, המערכת מייצרת task ל-replenishment.

בנוסף קיימים part replenishment creation ו-no order staging (פחות נפוצים).

**Configuration:**
1. **Define default values for deliveries** — IMG: Logistics Execution • Decentralized WMS Integration • Central Processing • Application • Inventory Management Interface and Delivery-Relevant Data • Define Default Values for Deliveries (Figure 2.58).
2. **Determine movement type** — IMG: Production • Shop Floor Control • Integration • Determine Movement Types (Figure 2.59).

sections.title: Consumption for Manufacturing Orders
sections.en: 2.3.2 Consumption for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the consumption process in advanced production integration. In short, a manufacturing order process in SAP entails tracking and recording the utilization of materials and resources throughout the production of goods. Business Process After products, batches, or HUs have been used in a manufacturing process, an important step is recording their consumption in both the SAP EWM and SAP ERP systems. This consistency helps you maintain accurate inventory levels and enables better planning of raw materials and components. SAP EWM provides an option for advanced production integration, which allows for consumption posting using RF or desktop transactions in SAP EWM. Consumption posting can be performed for the entire quantity of a product at once or for partial quantities at regular intervals, depending on the manufacturing process, as shown in Figure 2.90. You can also reverse consumption postings if needed. Over-quantity consumption refers to posting consumption for more of a product than was planned in the PMR, while partial consumption allows users to post consumption based on quantities that have already been used or on remaining quantities. Figure 2.90 Consumption for Manufacturing Order Process Demo Let’s delve into the step-by-step process for the consumption for manufacturing orders using the advanced production integration method: 1. Post consumption for a manufacturing order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To post the consumption for a manufacturing order, execute Transaction Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 120 /SCWM/RFUI. From the RF device menu, follow the path Outbound Processes • Consumption • Consumption by Manufacturing Order. Scan or enter the manufacturing order, then click on Enter. On the next screen, enter the consumption quantity, as shown in Figure 2.91, and press (Enter). A successful consumption posting updates the goods issue material document in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Figure 2.91 Posting Consumption for Manufacturing Order 2. Verify consumption posting /goods issue has updated in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To verify the consumption posting, execute Transaction COR3. As shown in Figure 2.92, enter a manufacturing order number and click Continue. On the next screen, follow the menu path More • Go To • Lists • Documented Goods Movements. The consumption posting document should appear with movement type 261. Figure 2.92 Verify Consumption Posting Note The production consumption process using advanced production integration is now complete. Note Warehouse users can post consumption for manufacturing orders via Transaction NWBC or via RF handheld devices. © 121

sections.title: Goods Receipt for Manufacturing Orders
sections.en: 2.3.3 Goods Receipt for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the goods receipt process for advanced production integration. In short, the goods receipt process for a manufacturing order in SAP involves the receipt and recording of finished goods into inventory after the completion of production. Business Process For goods receipts triggered from SAP EWM, when a manufacturing order is released in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, for decentralized Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (decentralized SAP EWM), the expected goods receipt is automatically generated by the system, as shown in Figure 2.93. This step triggers the creation of an inbound delivery via the desktop Transaction /SCWM/GRPI, followed by HU packing, the goods receipt, and the putaway warehouse task. Figure 2.93 Goods Receipt for Manufacturing Order In the RF-based option, a user scans a manufacturing order, which prompts the system to create an inbound delivery. Based on the user’s inputs, the material is packed, HUs are created, and automatic goods receipt takes place. Additionally, a warehouse putaway task is created based on PPF settings. Configuration In this section, we’ll discuss essential customization settings that are required for the goods receipt process in a manufacturing order. It is important to note Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 122 that prior customization of ERP and SAP EWM settings is necessary to ensure a seamless execution of this process. Follow these steps: 1. Configuring a document type for inbound delivery in SAP EWM The document type for inbound delivery can be configured via the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Inbound Delivery • Define Document Types for Inbound Delivery. Click New Entries and then maintain or check the configuration, as shown in Figure 2.94. Figure 2.94 Document Type for Inbound Delivery 2. Configuring an item type for inbound delivery in SAP EWM This item type for inbound delivery can be configured by following the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process Inbound Delivery • Manual Settings • Define Item Types for Inbound Delivery. To configure an item type for inbound delivery, click New Entries and then maintain or check the configuration, as shown in Figure 2.95. © 123 Figure 2.95 Item Type for Inbound Delivery 3. Define allowed document type and item types and item types for inbound delivery in SAP EWM This setting defines a document type and item types for inbound delivery. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Inbound Delivery • Define Allowed Item Types in Inbound Delivery Process. Click New Entries and then maintain or check the configuration, as shown in Figure 2.96. Figure 2.96 Allowed Document Type and Item Types 4. Configuring a reference document type profile for inbound delivery in SAP EWM This setting is for customer profile reference categories. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Delivery-Warehouse Request • Reference Documents • Define Reference Document Type Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 124 Profiles. To configure a reference document profile for inbound delivery, maintain the Cust. Profile (customer profile) and Sys. Profile (system profile) fields, as shown in Figure 2.97. Click Reference Document Categories and for the entry under Doc. Cat select the Inactive checkbox. Figure 2.97 Configuring Reference Document Type Profile 5. Configure an action and conditions for inbound delivery in SAP EWM This setting is for setting up an action and its conditions for inbound delivery. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross Process Setting • Delivery -Warehouse Request • Actions • Change Actions and Conditions • Define Action Profiles and Actions. To configure the action and its conditions, select the Action Profile, as shown in Figure 2.98. Double-click Action Definition. Verify that the action definition for the goods receipt post and warehouse task creation is active by ensuring that the Inactive checkbox is not selected. © 125 Figure 2.98 Configure Action and Conditions 6. Configure action scheduling for inbound delivery actions in SAP EWM This setting is for action scheduling for Inbound Delivery. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross Process Setting • Delivery -Warehouse Request • Action • Configure Action Scheduling • Maintain Determination Procedure. To configure action scheduling for inbound delivery, check the determination procedure for posting the goods receipt is ODMGR and create a warehouse task for ODMWT, as shown in Figure 2.99. Figure 2.99 Configure Action Scheduling Note Before configuring the action scheduling capability for inbound delivery actions in SAP EWM, make sure following prerequisite configurations were performed in the following sequence: Create a field catalogue Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 126 Create condition tables Create access sequences Create condition types 7. Configure assignment of determination procedure in SAP EWM This setting is for action scheduling for inbound delivery. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross Process Setting • Delivery -Warehouse Request • Action • Configure Action Scheduling • Assign Determination Procedure. To assign a determination procedure for a combination of warehouse, document category, and document type, and maintain or check the configuration settings, as shown in Figure 2.100. Figure 2.100 Configure Assignment of Determination Procedure 8. Define ERP document types for differentiating attributes in SAP EWM This setting is for creating different ERP document types. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Interfaces • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Define ERP Document Types for Differentiation Attribute. To define ERP document types for different attributes, click New Entries and add new entries or verify existing ones, as shown in Figure 2.101. © 127 Figure 2.101 Define ERP Document Types for Differentiating Attributes 9. Configure the mapping of document types in SAP EWM This setting is for mapping document types between ERP and SAP EWM. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Document Types from ERP System to SAP EWM. To map document types from your ERP system to SAP EWM, click New Entries and add new entries or verify existing ones, as shown in Figure 2.102. Figure 2.102 Configure Mapping of Document Types 10. Configure mapping of item types in SAP EWM This setting is for mapping item types between ERP and SAP EWM. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Item Types from ERP system to SAP EWM. To map item types from the ERP system to SAP EWM, click New Entries and add new entries or verify existing ones, as shown in Figure 2.103. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 128 Figure 2.103 Configure Mapping of Item Types 11. Configure mapping of date types in SAP EWM This setting is to map date types of ERP and SAP EWM. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Date Types from ERP System to SAP EWM. To map date types from the ERP system to SAP EWM, click New Entries or verify the existing entries, as shown in Figure 2.104. Figure 2.104 Configure Mapping of Date Types 12. Control message processing dependent on recipient in SAP EWM This setting is to control message processing that is dependent on recipient. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Control Message Processing Dependent on Recipient. For this mapping, click New Entries or verify the existing entries, as shown in Figure 2.105. © 129 Figure 2.105 Control Message Processing Dependent on Recipient Master Data Setup One master data setup task is needed for this process: maintaining the condition record for automatic warehouse task creation in SAP EWM. Figure 2.106 Maintain Condition Record for Automatic Warehouse Task Creation You can find this setting via the SAP Easy Access Menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Delivery Processing • Actions • Maintain Condition Records for PPF Schedule Conditions or use Transaction /SCWM/DLVPPFC. To maintain condition records for automatic warehouse task creation, enter the application and maintenance group and then click Execute. Next, click Warehouse, enter the warehouse number, and maintain the condition record, as shown in Figure 2.106. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 130 Process Demo Let’s delve into the step-by-step process steps needed for goods receipt using advanced production integration: 1. Create manufacturing order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create and release manufacturing orders, execute Transaction COR1. Then, enter the material and click Continue. Enter all the required details, such as material and storage location, to create the process order and click Save, as shown in Figure 2.107. Figure 2.107 Create Manufacturing Order 2. Receiving HUs from production in SAP EWM To receive HUs from production in SAP EWM, execute Transaction /SCWM/RFUI and follow the menu path Inbound Process • Receiving of Handling Units • Rec. HU by Manufacturing Order • Rec. HU by Order and follow the steps, as shown in Figure 2.108. On the third RF screen, scan or enter the work center details and press (Enter). On the next screen, enter the manufacturing order and and press (Enter). On the last screen, press (F2), enter the packaging material for HU, and press (Enter). The goods receipt for the inbound delivery will be performed in the background automatically. © 131 Figure 2.108 Receiving HU from Production 3. Verify post goods receipt in SAP EWM To verify a goods receipt in SAP EWM, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI, input the manufacturing order, and click Execute. Make sure the goods receipt status is Completed, as shown in Figure 2.109. Figure 2.109 Verify Post Goods Receipt 4. Create putaway warehouse task To create a putaway warehouse task, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. On this screen input a manufacturing order and click Execute. Select the line item and, in the header, select More • Inbound Delivery • Follow on Function • Warehouse Tasks. This step opens the warehouse task creation screen, where you can select a line item and click Create + Save. The warehouse task will be created, as shown in Figure 2.110. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 132 Figure 2.110 Create Putaway Warehouse Task 5. Confirm putaway warehouse task To confirm warehouse task, execute Transaction /SCWM/TO_CONF, input the warehouse task, and then select Confirm + Save. The warehouse task will be confirmed, as shown in Figure 2.111. Figure 2.111 Confirm Putaway Warehouse Task 6. Verify goods receipt was posted for process order To verify the consumption posting, execute Transaction COR3. As shown in Figure 2.112, enter the manufacturing order number and click Continue. On the next screen, follow the path More • Go To • Lists • Documented Goods Movements and verify the good receipt was posted. Note Production goods receipt process using advanced production integration is now complete. Figure 2.112 Verify Goods Receipt Got Posted © 133

sections.title: Clear Production Supply Area Bin for Manufacturing
sections.en: 2.3.4 Clear Production Supply Area Bin for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll provide a concise explanation of the clear production supply area (production returns) process in SAP for advanced production integration. In summary, the clear production supply area process for a manufacturing order involves returning any leftover materials that will not be used on the production lines back to the warehouse. Business Process After the production process is finished, if any leftover material does not require any other PMR, this material should be returned to the warehouse. This step is necessary to ensure that the material does not take up unnecessary space in the production staging area (production supply area) and can be easily retrieved later when needed. For single-order staged material in a production supply area, the reference document must be released to clear the reference in stock and clear the production supply area, as shown in Figure 2.113. Figure 2.113 Clear Production Supply Area Bin for Manufacturing Order Process Demo Let’s walk through the step-by-step process for the clearing production supply areas (production returns) in SAP for advanced production integration: 1. Set status for manufacturing order as technically completed (TECO) in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To set up a manufacturing order as technically completed, execute Transaction COR2, input manufacturing order details, and click Continue. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 134 On the next screen, follow the path More • Process Order • Functions • Restrict Processing • Complete Technically. The manufacturing order system’s status will be updated to TECO, as shown in Figure 2.114. Figure 2.114 Set TECO Status for Manufacturing Order 2. Check the status of a PMR as technically completed in SAP EWM To check the status of a PMR as technical completed, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON and follow the path Outbound • Documents. Then, double- click Production Material Request. Enter the manufacturing order details and click Execute. Check that the production status is Technically completed, as shown in Figure 2.115. 3. Clear the production supply area in SAP EWM and move the unused material from the production supply area to the warehouse To clear the production supply area with SAP NetWeaver, execute Transaction NWBC with the role SAP EWM: Warehouse Expert. Click Work Scheduling • Staging for Production • Clear Production Supply Area and then input a production supply area and a manufacturing order and click Execute. Select the line item for stock without a released PMR and click Create Warehouse Task, as shown in Figure 2.116. © 135 Figure 2.115 PMR Technically Completed Figure 2.116 Create Warehouse Task: Clear Production Supply Area 4. Confirm the material movement in SAP EWM To confirm the material movement (which confirms the warehouse task), execute Transaction /SCWM/MON and follow the path Document • Warehouse Task. Then, double-click Input Warehouse Order. Click Execute. Select the warehouse order line item, go to More Methods and click Confirm WO in the background, as shown in Figure 2.117. Figure 2.117 Confirm Warehouse Task Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 136 Note The clear production supply area process using advanced production integration is now complete.

sections.title: Create Part Replenishment Process
sections.en: 2.3.5 Create Part Replenishment Process In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the create part replenishment process for advanced production integration. In short, create part replenishment process refers to the procedure of generating replenishment requests to ensure an adequate supply of parts is always available in the production supply area. Business Process In SAP EWM, Create Part Replenishment is a process that helps ensure that there are sufficient inventory levels of parts available at production supply area to fulfill demand manufacturing order. In a production BOM, some raw materials or components may not be included in the single-order staging or cross-order staging process but may still need to be staged under specific circumstances. This scenario can be achieved either by pallet-based staging, based on predefined packaging specifications, or by staging a predefined quantity using Transaction /SCWM/PSASTAGE. When a manufacturing order is released, a PMR is generated to request the creation of a part for replenishment. This step triggers the creation of a warehouse task to pick the part from a storage location that maintains inventory for the material and stage it to the production supply area. Automation of the replenishment process is possible by setting parameters that determine when the inventory level falls below a certain quantity at the production supply area, prompting the system to initiate the replenishment process automatically. Overall, the create part replenishment process in SAP EWM helps ensure that inventory levels are optimized and that parts are available when needed for outbound processing or production processes. © 137 Configuration Let’s see step by step configuration for create part replenishment process: 1. Activate BC sets in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the BC sets required for create part replenishment will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path Tools • Customizing • Business Configuration Sets • Activation of BC Sets. To activate the BC sets, go to the IMG menu path. Enter the BC set /SCWM/PMR_CROSS_ORDER, as shown in Figure 2.118, and click Activate. Figure 2.118 Activate BC Sets 2. Configuring an item type for production in SAP EWM This item type determination can find this setting. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process • Production Material Request • Define Item Types for Production. Click New Entries; then maintain or verify the configuration, as shown in Figure 2.119. 3. Define allowed item type for production in SAP EWM The configuration for allowed item types for production can find. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process • Production Material Request • Define Allowed Item Type for Production. To maintain the configuration for allowed item types for production, click New Entries and maintain or verify the configuration, as shown in Figure 2.120. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 138 Figure 2.119 Configuring Item Type for Production Figure 2.120 Define Allowed Item Type for Production 4. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Interface • ERP Integration • Production • Map SAP ERP Order Type to EWM Item Type. sections.title: SAP Manufacturing Execution Integration
sections.en: 2.4 SAP Manufacturing Execution Integration In the process of manufacturing, companies utilize SAP ERP, SAP S/4HANA, or SAP EWM to send staging requests for components or raw materials and perform goods receipts. Additionally, customers may also employ third-party SAP Manufacturing Execution systems or SAP Manufacturing Execution systems during the staging and production goods receipt process
sections.he: בתהליך הייצור, חברות משתמשות ב-SAP ERP, ‏SAP S/4HANA, או SAP EWM לשליחת staging requests ל-components/חומרי גלם ולביצוע goods receipts. בנוסף, ייתכן שימוש במערכות SAP Manufacturing Execution צד-שלישי או SAP Manufacturing Execution בתהליכי ה-staging וה-production goods receipt.

sections.title: SAP Manufacturing Execution Triggered Staging to
sections.en: 2.4.1 SAP Manufacturing Execution Triggered Staging to Production In this scenario, the SAP Manufacturing Execution or SAP MII system initiates a request to prepare raw materials or components for a single order or a cross- order. This request can be triggered when the manufacturing order is released, or when SFC numbers are started or completed. The SAP Manufacturing Execution or SAP MII system request only contains SAP EWM relevant components, such as batch information for single-order staging, or specific information such as quantity and location (production supply area) for staging as shown in Figure 2.132. Once the request and components are staged at the production supply area, SAP EWM sends a notification to the SAP Manufacturing Execution/SAP MII system, updating the quantity information. Figure 2.132 SAP Manufacturing Execution Triggered Staging The benefits of SAP Manufacturing Execution-triggered staging include: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 146 SAP EWM and SAP Manufacturing Execution are seamlessly integrated out-of- the-box. Staging of components is initiated based on real demand determined by the production system. Specific steps can be supplied with components through various trigger actions. The pull method for staging is ideal for production processes with limited space in the production supply area, as opposed to the push method. Benefits of these features include streamlined processes, improved efficiency, and optimized use of available space. SAP Digital Manufacturing, as shown in Figure 2.133, can also be integrated with SAP EWM (SAP S/4HANA OP 1909 FPS1 and SAP Digital Manufacturing 2008) and supports following scenarios: Single-order staging provides sending a request for the components to be staged for a specific order to a warehouse managed with SAP EWM. Single-order staging Confirmation allows the transfer of stock change notification from SAP EWM to SAP Digital Manufacturing when the warehouse task of component staging is confirmed. Figure 2.133 SAP Digital Cloud Integration with SAP EWM © 147

sections.en: 2.4.2 Integrating SAP EWM to SAP Manufacturing Execution and SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence to Receive Goods from Production To establish a connection between SAP EWM and SAP Manufacturing Execution/SAP MII systems for receiving goods from production, there are several options available. These include: Integrating SAP EWM with SAP Manufacturing Execution via SAP ERP Directly integrating SAP EWM with SAP Manufacturing Execution Integrating SAP EWM with a SAP Manufacturing Execution system using SAP EWM API Receiving goods using SAP Manufacturing Execution Receiving goods using SAP MII Out of the above integration options for SAP EWM to SAP Manufacturing Execution and SAP MII, the SAP EWM API option in particular involves connecting the SAP EWM system to a SAP Manufacturing Execution system using an internal API, which provides a straightforward integration of the SAP EWM production process with SAP Manufacturing Execution. With this integration, the SAP Manufacturing Execution system notifies the SAP EWM system via API when the production for a pallet is finished. The SAP EWM system then performs the goods receipt process pallet by pallet, automatically creating inbound deliveries and HUs in the background. The Putaway warehouse task and confirmation of the warehouse task are completed automatically, based on the PPF setting as shown in Figure 2.134.
