sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 2.5 Summary That’s it! You’re ready to get started on your SAP Production Integration with SAP EWM. In this chapter, you explored how various Production Integration is integrated with Extended Warehouse Management. Various Production Integration methods such as delivery-based production integration and Advanced Production integration. You also deep dived various production process such as staging, consumption, create parts replenishment, Clear production supply area and goods receipt for manufacturing order. In addition to this, you also explored SAP Manufacturing execution integration, SAP Manufacturing Execution triggered staging for production. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 150 3 Quality Management Quality management is a pivotal component of SAP S/4HANA that enables businesses to implement and operate quality control processes with ease. It is crafted to prevent defects, foster continuous process improvement, and establish sustainable quality control programs. The aim of this chapter is to provide you with a comprehensive guide to various quality management processes and their seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM), especially with embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM). SAP EWM has the ability to integrate with quality management in order to guarantee adherence to quality standards during the storage and handling of goods. Organizations can reap numerous benefits from quality management, including compliance with manufacturing quality regulations, reduced operating costs, and enhanced customer satisfaction. The integration between SAP EWM and quality management allows for quality inspections to be conducted at various stages of the warehouse process, such as during goods receipt, putaway, and outbound processes. The result of this integration is the assurance that quality standards are met prior to the dispatch of products to customers. SAP EWM can activate quality inspections and apprise quality management of the outcomes, thereby allowing quality management to create quality notifications or update inspection lots. The integration also facilitates the monitoring of quality-related data throughout the warehouse process, granting organizations visibility into quality-related key performance indicators (KPIs) and enabling data-driven decisions. This chapter examines various aspects of quality management integration and different quality management business processes that can be integrated with SAP EWM. The introductory section provides a synopsis of quality management in SAP EWM, followed by an analysis of different quality management processes such as the inspection of material and batch during an inbound delivery in SAP. This process is further categorized into the inspection of material for externally procured and in-house inspection. Furthermore, this chapter delves into another quality management process, internal warehouse inspection, which is further divided into stock inspection and recurring inspection for batches. Finally, this chapter provides in-depth coverage of the advanced returns management process with quality inspection. ©
sections.he: סיכום. בפרק זה חקרנו כיצד שיטות production integration שונות משולבות עם Extended Warehouse Management — ‏delivery-based production integration ו-advanced production integration. צללנו לתהליכי ייצור שונים: ‏staging, ‏consumption, ‏create part replenishment, ‏clear production supply area, ו-goods receipt ל-manufacturing order. בנוסף חקרנו את שילוב SAP Manufacturing Execution ואת ה-staging המופעל ע"י SAP Manufacturing Execution.

sections.title: Overview of Quality Management in SAP EWM
sections.en: 3.1 Overview of Quality Management in SAP EWM In this section, we’ll present an overview of quality management in SAP EWM, including its architecture and deployment options. We’ll discuss the key terminology used with quality management, then dive into the strategy for maintaining inspection rules. SAP EWM employs a thorough quality management system that comprises diverse processes, procedures, and tools to guarantee the conformity of stored goods and materials with the appropriate quality standards and to ensure that warehouse operations meet the required standards. The main goal of quality management in SAP EWM is to ensure uniform product quality, minimize the risk of defects and errors, and enhance customer satisfaction. The essential elements of quality management in SAP EWM encompass quality inspection, quality control, quality documentation, non- conformance management, and continuous improvement. SAP EWM’s quality management functionality guarantees products received and packaging meet your quality criteria. The Quality Inspection Engine is utilized to execute inspection processes in the warehouse. The Quality Inspection Engine can be employed to conduct quality inspections exclusively in SAP EWM or can be merged with the Quality Management (QM) component of SAP ERP if you have previously configured it. For more intricate quality management procedures, the Quality Inspection Engine can be linked to an external quality management system, like QM in SAP ERP, that includes comprehensive analytical inspections and characteristics. Once an inspection document is initiated in SAP EWM, the Quality Inspection Engine prompts the creation of an inspection lot in the quality management function of the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The inspection procedure is then performed in the external system, which is the ERP quality management system. Once the inspection process is completed, the ERP quality management transmits the usage decision back to the Quality Inspection Engine. This option is available for both SAP EWM connected to ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems, whether they are SAP S/4HANA or non-SAP S/4HANA (ERP). Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 152 As shown in Figure 3.1, the Quality Inspection Engine, within the context of software architecture, refers to a layer of software components that exist in the SAP EWM software stack. This software stack, when integrated with QM in SAP ERP, forms a simplified SAP EWM software stack. Figure 3.1 Quality Inspection Engine Software Stack In SAP EWM, the available options for quality management include the following: Embedded EWM As shown in Figure 3.2, with this option, quality management and extended warehouse management (EWM) functionalities are hosted on the same server as SAP S/4HANA. This integration eliminates the need for data transfers between systems. Figure 3.2 Embedded EWM Option ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM on SAP S/4HANA As shown in Figure 3.3, beginning with SAP S/4HANA 1809 Feature Package Stack © 153 (FPS) 02, you can utilize quality management features alongside SAP ERP for executing quality inspections in a decentralized extended warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA (decentralized EWM). This alternative employs the Quality Inspection Engine within SAP EWM, allowing quality management procedures to be executed similarly to those in the central SAP ERP instance. ERP or SAP S/4HANA with SAP EWM 9.5 or lower version (decentralized) With this option, as shown in Figure 3.4, you can use the quality management function in SAP ERP to perform quality inspections in a decentralized warehouse using SAP EWM (for EWM on a non-SAP S/4HANA system). The Quality Inspection Engine in SAP EWM can be utilized similarly to the central ERP instance when using quality management. Figure 3.3 EWM on SAP S/4HANA Options Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 154 Figure 3.4 SAP EWM 9.5 or Lower Role and importance of quality processes and functions in SAP EWM Embedded EWM incorporates quality management processes and functions to support various operations such as external and in-house production goods inspection, internal warehouse inspections, and customer return processes. The following processes and functions are supported: Processes: Inspection of goods procured externally, which includes inspection after goods receipt, acceptance sampling, goods receipt control, and first article inspection Inspections of goods from in-house production, which includes pre-sampling in production and inspection after goods receipt Internal warehouse inspections, which include stock inspections and recurring inspections Customer returns process, which includes customer return process with return material authorizations (RMAs) Functions: Partial quantity decision Inspection lot/document summary Available-to-promise (ATP)/material requirements planning (MRP) integration Dynamic modification/skip lot © 155 Link between inspection lot and material document in goods receipt Display of inspection lots and documents in the warehouse monitor Integration to defect and quality notifications Quality management in decentralized EWM facilitates the following inspection processes: Inspections for goods receipt processes: Inspection of handling units (HUs) Counting of delivered products Inspection of products received from suppliers Inspection of products from customer returns Inspection of externally procured or internally produced goods before goods receipt Inspection of externally procured or internally produced goods after goods receipt Inspections in the warehouse Inspection of stock not related to a delivery Periodic inspection of batch-managed products Inspections for returns Inspection of returned goods from customers Inspection of customer returns using advanced returns management Other functionalities include Creation of inspection lots in SAP ERP based on inspection documents from the Quality Inspection Engine Recording of results in quality management in SAP ERP based on quality management inspection plans Replication of usage decisions to SAP EWM Follow-up actions in SAP EWM based on usage decisions Table 3.1 shows the differences between the available deployment options for SAP EWM. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 156 Feature Embedded EWM Decentralized EWM SAP EWM 9.5 Quality Inspection Engine for quality management processes with ERP quality management integration, as well as standalone processes without ERP quality management integration Not applicable Supported with restriction Supported Quality Inspection Engine standalone process: Preliminary inbound delivery inspection (IOT1) Not applicable Not supported, not strategic Supported With ERP quality management integration: Automatic creation of separate Not applicable Planned for future release Currently not supported, planned with a future release. For now, manual warehouse Not supported (Warehouse task for sample quantity can be created manually with support from business add-in [BAdI] /SCWM/EX_WRKC_PACK_QTY_PROPOSE.) © 157 Feature Embedded EWM Decentralized EWM SAP EWM 9.5 warehouse tasks to move sample quality to an inspection area task creation option for sample quantity With ERP quality management integration: Quality Inspection Engine document attachment Not applicable Not supported, not strategic Supported With ERP quality management integration non-100% inspection procedure Not applicable Not supported, not strategic Supported With ERP quality management integration: Dynamic modification in the Quality Inspection Engine Not applicable Not supported, not strategic Supported Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 158 Feature Embedded EWM Decentralized EWM SAP EWM 9.5 inspection rule Counting inbound delivery (IOT2) Not supported Supported Supported Preliminary inspection HU (IOT6) Not supported Supported Supported Table 3.1 Deployment Options for SAP EWM with Quality Process Next, we’ll discuss some key terminology. In SAP EWM, quality management encompasses the utilization of several essential concepts to handle goods inspections and uphold quality. Let’s consider the following terms: Inspection object types An inspection object type refers to the software component, process, and object for which an inspection document can be created in the Quality Inspection Engine. Different types of inspection object types, including Preliminary Inspection of Inbound delivery (IOT1), Counting Inbound delivery (IOT2), Q-Inspection of Return delivery (IOT3), Q-Inspection Product/Batch Inbound delivery (IOT4), Q-Inspection of Product/ Batch Warehouse – Internal (IOT5), and Preliminary Inspection of Handling Unit (IOT6). Note As per SAP Note 2861813, inspection object types IOT1, IO2 and IOT6 will no longer be supported by embedded EWM systems, whereas for embedded EWM the return processing (formally IOT3) was integrated to advanced returns management. Inspection types Inspection types are used to define the controls associated with each inspection. The type of inspection determines how an inspection is carried out. Inspection rules Inspection rules, on the other hand, provide guidelines for creating an inspection document. These rules are assigned to inspection object types and determine if an © 159 object (delivery, product, or batch) will be subject to quality inspections or not. Some characteristics of inspection rules include an inspection procedure (e.g., 100% inspection versus no inspection), a sample drawing procedure, dynamic modifications, and document types. In a decentralized system, the SAP EWM module in SAP S/4HANA is responsible for quality management using inspection rules. These rules are maintained as master data, and inspection documents are created in the SAP EWM system based on this data. Additionally, an inspection lot is generated in the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. With the release of SAP S/4HANA 1909, inspection rules can now be automatically synchronized from an ERP or SAP S/4HANA system, thus streamlining the process even further, as shown in Figure 3.5. In a decentralized EWM system (version 9.5 or below) and where SAP S/4HANA is not used, quality management in SAP EWM is carried out using inspection rules. These rules are maintained as master data, and inspection documents are created in the SAP EWM system based on this data. Additionally, an inspection lot is generated in the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system, as shown in Figure 3.6. Figure 3.5 Decentralized EWM: Inspection Rule Figure 3.6 Decentralized EWM: Inspection Rule (SAP EWM 9.5 or Lower) An embedded EWM system can perform quality management using inspection rules or not, as shown in Table 3.2. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 160 With Inspection Rules Without Inspection Rules EWM is integrated into the quality management component using inspection lots of origin 17. EWM is integrated into the quality management component using inspection lots of origin 17. An active inspection rule is required, and the inspection data has to be setup. The inspection settings of the Quality Management tab in the material master are used. Only possible in embedded EWM; not applicable to decentralized EWM. Can be used in the following processes: acceptance sampling, inspection after goods receipt, pre-sampling in production, stock inspections, and recurring inspections. Table 3.2 Embedded EWM with and without Inspection Rules Inspection setup Inspection lots are generated for all goods movements that are pertinent to quality management. The material master determines which goods movements are relevant to quality management. In the quality management module, inspections can be planned, and all materials can be prepared at this stage. Each material can be assigned appropriate inspection types, and the inspection configuration can be modified as required. The inspection setup in decentralized EWM is shown in Figure 3.7. Figure 3.7 Inspection Setup in Decentralized EWM © 161 The inspection setup in embedded EWM is shown in Figure 3.8. Figure 3.8 Inspection Setup in Embedded EWM Decision codes Using decision codes, you can indicate whether a sample is accepted, assign a quality score, and specify any necessary follow-up actions. These codes are organized into code groups, which are subsequently linked to inspection rules in a hierarchical manner (inspection rules < decision groups < decision codes). Findings During the processing of an inspection document, inspection outcomes can be documented in the form of characteristic values or findings. The requirements for findings would depend on the item being inspected and the type of inspection being conducted. Follow-up sections You can initiate a series of follow-up processes, such as putaway, stock transfer, scrapping, or return delivery, by employing logical actions. These logical actions will generate warehouse documents and tasks. Data model of the Quality Inspection Engine (for inspection rules) A data model of how the Quality Inspection Engine works is shown in Figure 3.9. Figure 3.9 Quality Inspection Engine Data Model Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 162 The inspection object type serves to define the business process for inspections; the object to be inspected (e.g., product, HU, or delivery); and the warehouse number. Each inspection object type can have multiple inspection rules, which determine the criteria for triggering inspections and specify inspection details such as the process, procedure, frequency, and codes. During the inspection process, the system creates multiple inspection documents based on the inspection rules. These documents contain the inspection specifications and are used to collect inspection results, findings, and usage decisions for the inspected object. Each inspection document can have multiple items and samples assigned to it, and there can be multiple findings associated with each document. However, there can only be one decision. A follow-up action, such as putaway or scrapping, can be assigned to the usage decision. © 163
sections.he:
‏SAP EWM מפעיל מערכת quality management מקיפה המורכבת מתהליכים, נהלים וכלים שונים להבטחת התאמת הסחורה והחומרים המאוחסנים לתקני האיכות. המטרה: אחידות איכות, מזעור סיכון לפגמים, ושיפור שביעות רצון הלקוח. הרכיבים: ‏quality inspection, ‏quality control, ‏quality documentation, ‏non-conformance management, ו-continuous improvement.

ה-**Quality Inspection Engine** מבצע תהליכי inspection במחסן. ניתן להשתמש בו בלעדית ב-SAP EWM, או למזגו עם רכיב ה-Quality Management (QM) של SAP ERP. לתהליכים מורכבים יותר, ה-Quality Inspection Engine ניתן לחיבור למערכת quality management חיצונית (כגון QM ב-SAP ERP). עם יצירת inspection document ב-SAP EWM, ה-Quality Inspection Engine מפעיל יצירת inspection lot ב-QM של ה-ERP; ה-inspection מתבצע במערכת החיצונית, וה-usage decision מוחזר ל-Quality Inspection Engine. זמין הן ל-SAP EWM המחובר ל-SAP S/4HANA והן ל-ERP שאינו-S/4HANA.

‏Figure 3.1 — ה-Quality Inspection Engine הוא שכבת רכיבי תוכנה בתוך ה-SAP EWM software stack. בשילוב עם QM ב-SAP ERP, נוצר stack מפושט.

אפשרויות quality management:
• **Embedded EWM** (Figure 3.2) — QM ו-EWM מתארחים על אותו שרת כמו SAP S/4HANA. אין צורך בהעברות נתונים.
• **ERP/S4HANA + SAP EWM על SAP S/4HANA** (Figure 3.3) — מ-SAP S/4HANA 1809 FPS02, ניתן להשתמש ב-QM יחד עם SAP ERP לביצוע inspections ב-decentralized EWM, באמצעות ה-Quality Inspection Engine.
• **ERP/S4HANA עם SAP EWM 9.5 ומטה (decentralized)** (Figure 3.4) — שימוש ב-QM של SAP ERP לביצוע inspections במחסן מבוזר (EWM על מערכת שאינה-S/4HANA).

‏embedded EWM משלב תהליכי QM: inspection של goods חיצוניים ומיוצרים-פנים, internal warehouse inspections, ותהליכי customer return. תהליכים נתמכים: inspection של goods שנרכשו חיצונית (after GR, ‏acceptance sampling, ‏GR control, ‏first article inspection); ‏inspections של goods מ-in-house production (pre-sampling, ‏after GR); ‏internal warehouse inspections (stock inspections, ‏recurring); ‏customer returns עם return material authorizations (RMAs). פונקציות: partial quantity decision, ‏inspection lot/document summary, שילוב ATP/MRP, ‏dynamic modification/skip lot, קישור בין inspection lot ל-material document, תצוגה ב-warehouse monitor, שילוב ל-defect ו-quality notifications.

‏QM ב-decentralized EWM מקל על: inspections ל-GR (HUs, ספירת מוצרים, מוצרים מספקים, customer returns, goods לפני/אחרי GR); ‏inspections במחסן (stock לא-קשור-delivery, ‏periodic של batch-managed); ‏inspections להחזרות. בנוסף: יצירת inspection lots ב-SAP ERP על בסיס inspection documents מה-Quality Inspection Engine, רישום תוצאות ב-QM של SAP ERP, שכפול usage decisions ל-SAP EWM, ו-follow-up actions.

‏Table 3.1 — הבדלי deployment options ל-SAP EWM עם QM:

| Feature | Embedded | Decentralized | SAP EWM 9.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| QIE עם/בלי שילוב ERP QM | לא ישים | נתמך עם הגבלה | נתמך |
| QIE standalone: Preliminary inbound delivery inspection (IOT1) | לא ישים | לא נתמך (לא אסטרטגי) | נתמך |
| יצירה אוטומטית של warehouse tasks להזזת sample לאזור inspection | לא ישים | מתוכנן לעתיד (כרגע ידני) | לא נתמך (task ל-sample ניתן ליצירה ידנית עם BAdI /SCWM/EX_WRKC_PACK_QTY_PROPOSE) |
| QIE document attachment | לא ישים | לא נתמך | נתמך |
| Non-100% inspection procedure | לא ישים | לא נתמך | נתמך |
| Dynamic modification ב-QIE inspection rule | לא ישים | לא נתמך | נתמך |
| Counting inbound delivery (IOT2) | לא נתמך | נתמך | נתמך |
| Preliminary inspection HU (IOT6) | לא נתמך | נתמך | נתמך |

**Table 3.1** ‏deployment options עם תהליך QM

**מינוח מפתח:**
• **Inspection object types** — רכיב התוכנה, התהליך והאובייקט שעבורם נוצר inspection document. סוגים: ‏IOT1 (Preliminary Inspection of Inbound delivery), ‏IOT2 (Counting Inbound delivery), ‏IOT3 (Q-Inspection of Return delivery), ‏IOT4 (Q-Inspection Product/Batch Inbound delivery), ‏IOT5 (Q-Inspection Product/Batch Warehouse-Internal), ‏IOT6 (Preliminary Inspection of HU). לפי SAP Note 2861813, ‏IOT1/IOT2/IOT6 לא ייתמכו עוד ב-embedded EWM; ה-return processing (לשעבר IOT3) שולב ב-advanced returns management.
• **Inspection types** — מגדירים את הבקרות לכל inspection וקובעים כיצד מבוצע.
• **Inspection rules** — הנחיות ליצירת inspection document. משויכים ל-IOTs וקובעים אם אובייקט (delivery/product/batch) יעבור inspection. מאפיינים: ‏inspection procedure (100% מול ללא), ‏sample drawing procedure, ‏dynamic modifications, ‏document types.

ב-decentralized, מודול ה-SAP EWM ב-SAP S/4HANA אחראי ל-QM באמצעות inspection rules (master data); ‏inspection documents נוצרים ב-SAP EWM, ו-inspection lot נוצר ב-ERP/S4HANA. מ-SAP S/4HANA 1909, ניתן לסנכרן inspection rules אוטומטית מ-ERP/S4HANA (Figure 3.5). ב-decentralized 9.5 ומטה (ללא S/4HANA), אותו עקרון (Figure 3.6).

‏embedded EWM יכול לבצע QM עם או בלי inspection rules (Table 3.2):

| With Inspection Rules | Without Inspection Rules |
|---|---|
| EWM משולב ב-QM דרך inspection lots of origin 17 | EWM משולב ב-QM דרך inspection lots of origin 17 |
| נדרש inspection rule פעיל + הגדרת inspection data | נעשה שימוש בהגדרות ה-Quality Management tab ב-material master |
| — | רק ב-embedded EWM, לא ב-decentralized |
| — | ניתן לשימוש ב: acceptance sampling, after GR, pre-sampling, stock inspections, recurring |

**Table 3.2** ‏embedded EWM עם/בלי inspection rules

**Inspection setup** — ‏inspection lots נוצרים לכל goods movement רלוונטי-QM. ה-material master קובע אילו רלוונטיים. כל material משויך ל-inspection types (Figures 3.7 decentralized, 3.8 embedded).
**Decision codes** — מציינים אם sample מתקבל, מקצים quality score, ומגדירים follow-up actions. מאורגנים ב-code groups, מקושרים היררכית ל-inspection rules (inspection rules < decision groups < decision codes).
**Findings** — תוצאות inspection מתועדות כ-characteristic values או findings.
**Follow-up sections** — יוזמים תהליכי המשך (putaway, ‏stock transfer, ‏scrapping, ‏return delivery) דרך logical actions, היוצרים warehouse documents ו-tasks.

**Data model** (Figure 3.9) — ה-IOT מגדיר את התהליך, האובייקט (product/HU/delivery), וה-warehouse number. לכל IOT inspection rules מרובים. במהלך ה-inspection נוצרים inspection documents מרובים (specifications, results, findings, usage decisions). לכל document items ו-samples מרובים, ו-findings מרובים, אך החלטה אחת בלבד; ל-usage decision ניתן לשייך follow-up action.

sections.title: Inspection Product/Batch for Inbound
sections.en: 3.2 Inspection Product/Batch for Inbound Deliveries SAP EWM offers various inspection processes for product/batch inbound delivery, such as the following: Inspection after goods receipt from external procurement (with inspection rule) In this process, individual products or batches are subject to inspection during the goods receipt process, controlled by inspection object type IOT4. Pre-sampling in production or inspection after goods receipt (SAP EWM 9.2 and higher) Pre-sampling is a process utilized for internally produced goods in SAP EWM. Acceptance sampling (SAP EWM 9.2 and higher) Before posting a goods receipt for externally procured goods, a necessary step is to conduct a quality inspection. Acceptance sampling can be used to determine whether to allow or block a goods receipt and, if allowed, whether to impose restrictions until a usage decision is made. If a restricted goods receipt is allowed, the stock category for the goods receipt posting (e.g., blocked stock) can be defined through the configuration of the follow-up action. Additionally, acceptance sampling can be combined with inspection control after goods receipt. For example, based on the acceptance sample result, a decision can be made to allow a restricted goods receipt into blocked stock, followed by a more detailed inspection after goods receipt. To combine acceptance sampling with inspection control after goods receipt, an inspection rule must be maintained for both acceptance sampling and inspections after goods receipt. We’ll discuss the first two options in more depth in the following sections. Because acceptance sampling is not commonly used, we won’t cover that topic further in this chapter. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 164
sections.he:
‏SAP EWM מציע תהליכי inspection שונים ל-product/batch inbound delivery:
• **Inspection after GR from external procurement (עם inspection rule)** — products/batches עוברים inspection בעת ה-GR, נשלט ע"י IOT4.
• **Pre-sampling in production או inspection after GR** (SAP EWM 9.2+) — ‏pre-sampling ל-goods מיוצרים-פנים.
• **Acceptance sampling** (SAP EWM 9.2+) — לפני רישום GR ל-goods שנרכשו חיצונית, מבוצע quality inspection. קובע אם לאפשר/לחסום GR, ואם לאפשר — אם להטיל הגבלות עד ל-usage decision. ניתן לשלב עם inspection control after GR (למשל GR מוגבל ל-blocked stock, ואחריו inspection מפורט). ל-acceptance sampling דרוש inspection rule לשני התהליכים.

נדון בהרחבה בשתי האפשרויות הראשונות. ‏acceptance sampling פחות נפוץ ולא יכוסה כאן.

sections.title: Inspection after Goods Receipts from External
sections.en: 3.2.1 Inspection after Goods Receipts from External Procurement (With Inspection Rule) The inspection process following the receipt of goods from external procurement with inspection rule is available in SAP EWM 5.0 and higher. Individual products or batches are subject to inspection during the goods receipt process, controlled by IOT4. Depending on the system configuration, the inspection document is generated either upon activation of the inbound delivery or when the inbound delivery status is set to In Yard. In this section, we’ll cover the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for inspections after goods receipt from external procurement with an inspection rule. We’ll then walk you step-by-step through a process demo. Business Scenario As shown in Figure 3.10, an inspection process is initiated in SAP EWM in one of two ways: activating an inbound delivery or setting the In Yard status. Figure 3.10 Inspection after Goods Receipt: External Procurement Once triggered, the process follows these steps: In SAP EWM, the goods receipt for the inbound delivery is completed. Upon completing the full goods receipt or the first partial goods receipt, SAP EWM releases the inspection document. 1 2 © 165 SAP EWM prompts ERP or SAP S/4HANA to generate a corresponding inspection lot with lot origin 17 (external) in the quality management module of ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Based on the quality management configuration in ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the system calculates the sample size. Information received from ERP or SAP S/4HANA is used to update the inspection document in SAP EWM with the inspection lot number and sample size. The user conducts the inspection process, result recording, and usage decision. The user records the results and usage decision in the quality management module of ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The inspection results are automatically updated in the inspection document in SAP EWM in the background. Depending on the decision code, the ERP system or SAP SAP S/4HANA may trigger a logistical follow-up action. This step is optional. Configuration In order to execute this process, several prerequisite customization settings must be configured. The following settings are the most important ones required for this process: 1. Specify a work center layout in SAP EWM In this setting, a work center layout will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Work Center • Specify Work Center Layout. To specify a work center layout, click New Entries and maintain Work Center Layout YQIC for your warehouse numbers, as shown in Figure 3.11. 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 166 Alternatively, you can verify the existing configuration settings according to your business requirements. Figure 3.11 Specify Work Center Layout 2. Define a work center in SAP EWM In this setting, a work center will be defined.A work center represents a physical area designated for quality engineers to perform various functions related to an inspection lot. These functions include the following: Recording inspection results Making usage decisions based on the inspection results Repacking partial quantities into new destination HUs and closing them Printing HU labels when using the partial quantity decision functionality Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Work Center • Define Work Center. To define a work center, click New Entries and maintain work center QUAL for your warehouse numbers, as shown in Figure 3.12. Alternatively, you can verify the existing configuration settings according to your business requirements. © 167 Figure 3.12 Define Work Center 3. Assign a default work center for inspection in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, a work center will be assigned for inspection. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Assign Default Work Center for Inspections. To assign a default work center for inspection, select a work center for warehouse 1804 and assign the work center QUAL, as shown in Figure 3.13. Figure 3.13 Assign Default Work Center for Inspection 4. Define process-oriented storage control (POSC) in SAP EWM Dedicated quality teams typically handle quality functions in real-world scenarios from quality centers. In SAP EWM, a material flow can be configured to send pallets requiring inspection to these centers upon goods Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 168 receipt. After the quality inspection, the sample pallets can be directed to either the final putaway area or the scrapping area, depending on the inspection results. To meet this business requirement in SAP EWM, POSC can be utilized. POSC unloads the material first, then directs the pallets requiring inspection to the quality center, and finally carries out the final putaway in the warehouse. In this configuration setting, POSC for quality inspection will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Warehouse Task • Define Process-Oriented Storage Control. Next, click Process- Oriented Storage Control and then New Entries. Now, maintain the assignment of external steps YPUT and YQIS to warehouse 1804, as shown in Figure 3.14. Click Save. Alternatively, you can verify the existing configuration settings according to your business requirements. Figure 3.14 Process-Oriented Storage Control Once POSC configuration is complete, the next step is to assign storage process steps. On the same screen, click Storage Process – Definition. Select the line item with the warehouse and storage process details and click the Assign Storage Process Step item on the right side of the screen. On the next screen, define the sequence for external steps YIUL, YQIS, and YIPW, as shown in Figure 3.15. © 169 Figure 3.15 Assign Storage Process Step 5. Define and activate warehouse-dependent inspection object types in SAP EWM When performing inspections after goods receipt, the IOT4 is typically used. In this case, inspection planning is carried out on the item level of the inbound delivery. In this configuration setting, the warehouse-dependent inspection object type setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent IOT’S. To define and activate warehouse-dependent inspection object types, click New Entries. Then, in the Insp Obj Type field, enter “4” and select the checkboxes needed under Warehouse-Dependent IOT Settings, as shown in Figure 3.16. Alternatively, you can verify the existing configuration settings according to your business requirements. Figure 3.16 Warehouse-Dependent Inspection Object Type Setting Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 170 6. Generate an inspection object types version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be generated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Generate Inspection Object Types Version. To generate an inspection object type version, select an IOT line item and click Generate New Version, as shown in Figure 3.17. Figure 3.17 Generation of Inspection Object Type Versions 7. Maintain an inspection object types version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Maintain Inspection Object Types Version. To maintain an inspection object type version, select an IOT version line item and select the Activ. IOT checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.18. Figure 3.18 Maintain Inspection Object Type Version 8. Maintain a follow-up action for quality control in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, a follow-up action after quality inspection will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Define and Activate Warehouse • Maintain Follow-Up Actions. To maintain follow-up © 171 actions for quality control, click New Entries and maintain the configuration for the follow-up action in SAP EWM, as shown in Figure 3.19. Alternatively, you can verify the existing configuration settings according to your business requirements. Figure 3.19 Define Follow-Up Action for Inspection Results Then, select the follow-up action line item and click Function Modules on the left side of the screen. Click New Entries and add function module QFOA_EWM_LOG_FOLLOW_UP_S4, as shown in Figure 3.20. Click Save. Figure 3.20 Follow-Up Action Function Module Maintain the more follow-up actions according to your business requirements. 9. Assign logistical follow-up actions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, logistical follow up actions will be assigned. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Define and Activate Warehouse • Maintain Follow-Up Actions •Assign Logistical Follow-up Actions. To assign logical follow up action, select the line item for follow-up action and click Assign Logistical Follow-Up Action on the left side of the screen. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 172 Then, maintain configuration settings for follow-up action EWM_A (Follow- Up Actn) for inspection object type 4 (Insp. Obj Type), as shown in Figure 3.21, for your warehouse. Click Save. Figure 3.21 Assign Logistical Follow-Up Action 10. Edit code groups and codes for usage decisions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, code groups and codes will be defined for representing usage decisions to standardize the options available to quality engineers when completing an inspection lot. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Completion • Edit Code Groups and Codes for Usage Decisions. Select the code group from the code group catalog or add your own code groups. Then, click Code Groups for Usage Decision on the left side of the screen, as shown in Figure 3.22. Figure 3.22 Codes for Usage Decision 11. Edit selected sets for usage decisions for usage decisions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, you’ll bundle code groups and codes that are required or allowed for a specific purpose at the plant level. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Completion • Edit Selected Sets for Usage Decisions. To edit selected code of usage decisions, select the plant and select the set line item. Then, click Selected Set Codes for Usage Decision on the left side of the screen. © 173 Click New Entries and maintain Code Group UD1701 and Code A1 and R1 configuration, as shown in Figure 3.23. Click Save. Figure 3.23 Selected Set Codes for Usage Decision 12. Maintain inspection types in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, inspection types needed for quality process will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Maintain Inspection Types. To maintain inspection types, click New Entries and maintain configuration for the inspection type 1701, as shown in Figure 3.24. 13. Define default values for inspection types in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, default values for inspection types will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Define Default Values for Inspection Type. To define default value for inspection type, select the line item for the inspection type for your process and click the Details tab. Verify the configuration settings, as shown in Figure 3.25. Figure 3.24 Maintain Inspection Types Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 174 Figure 3.25 Default Values for Inspection Type 14. Maintain settings at the plant level in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, plant-dependent quality management settings will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Basic Settings • Maintain Settings at Plant Level. To maintain settings at the plant level, select plant line items and click Inspection Type-Specific Settings for Plant on the left side of the screen. Click New Entries and maintain the configuration settings for Inspection type 01 and for UD plant 1804, as shown in Figure 3.26. Click Save. Figure 3.26 Inspection Type setting for Plant 15. Define warehouse process types in SAP EWM Since this business scenario is configured with POSC, a crucial step is to consider the warehouse type configuration. In this configuration setting, a warehouse process type will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Warehouse Task • Define Warehouse Process Type. To define a warehouse process type, click New Entries and set up the Warehouse Process Type Y010 and activity PTWY, as shown in Figure 3.27. © 175 Figure 3.27 Define Warehouse Process Type 16. Determine the warehouse process type in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the warehouse process type will be determined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings• Warehouse Task • Determine Warehouse Process Type. To determine warehouse process types, click New Entries and maintain the Determination of Warehouse Process Type table, for instance, Y010 for document type INB and item category IDLV, as shown in Figure 3.28. Figure 3.28 Determination of Warehouse Process Type 17. Specify storage type search sequence for putaway in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the storage type search sequence for putaway will be determined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage Type Search • Specify Storage Type Search Sequence for Putaway. To specify a storage type search sequence for putaway, click New Entries and set up Search Sequence: Putaway PUTW for Putaway Indicator (Ptwy) PUTW, as shown in Figure 3.29. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 176 Figure 3.29 Search Sequence Putaway 18. Activate business transaction event QBEXT in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, business transaction event QBEXT will be activated for quality process. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Environment • Tools • Communication with Quality Inspection Engines • Activation of Events for Transferring QM Data in Procurement • Activation of BTE Application. To activate a business transaction event, select Settings • Identification • SAP Applications. A popup message will appear that reads “Caution: The table is cross-client.” Click OK. Verify that application ID QBEXT is active, as shown in Figure 3.30. Follow the same process to activate application ID QBEXTP (External Inspection Procurement). Figure 3.30 BTE Application Indicator Master Data Setup Let’s go through the master data setting required for this process: 1. Inspection rules in SAP EWM The guidelines outlined in inspection rules dictate how to generate an inspection document. If any active inspection object types are related to a particular process and object, the inspection document will be automatically created using the inspection rules. To maintain inspection © 177 rules in SAP EWM, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Quality Management • Maintain Inspection Rule or use Transaction SCWM/QRSETUP. Click Create. Then, select a line item, select form view, and maintain the Inspection Rule for Document Type INB and Product, as shown in Figure 3.31. In addition, you must maintain an inspection type and inspection type details on this screen according to your business process. Figure 3.31 Inspection Rule for Inbound Delivery 2. Inspection plans in SAP EWM An inspection plan is utilized to specify the characteristics that must be inspected during each inspection operation and to identify the test equipment used during inspection. To maintain inspection plans in SAP EWM, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Inspection Planning • Create or use Transaction QP01. Input a material and a plant and click Continue. Then, maintain an inspection plan for material, usage, and plant, as shown in Figure 3.32. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 178 Figure 3.32 Maintain Inspection Plan 3. Define master data attributes for work centers in SAP EWM Define master data attributes for work centers by following the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data Work Center • Define Master Data Attributes or use Transaction /SCWM/TWORKST. Assign the Storage Bin to the Work Center, as shown in Figure 3.33. Figure 3.33 Define Master Data Attributes 4. Maintain warehouse product in SAP EWM In this master data setting maintain warehouse product: Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product • Maintain Warehouse Product or Transaction /SCWM/MAT1. To maintain warehouse product in SAP EWM, maintain the Process Type Determination Indicator and Putaway Control Indicator fields, as shown in Figure 3.34. © 179 Figure 3.34 Maintain Warehouse Product Process Demo In this section, we’ll outline the crucial procedural steps required for inspections for inbound deliveries after goods receipt in an external procurement business process. Follow these steps: 1. Create an inbound delivery referencing the corresponding purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create an inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL31N. Then, maintain the Supplier and Purchase Order fields, among other details, as per your business requirements and click Continue. On the next screen, enter material, quantity, and batch details, as shown in Figure 3.35. Click Save. Note the inbound delivery number, which you’ll need for the next step. Figure 3.35 Display Inbound Delivery 2. Display an inbound delivery in SAP EWM To display an inbound delivery, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI, enter an inbound delivery from your SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system in Inbound Delivery field and click Search. Verify material, batch, and inbound delivery details, as shown in Figure 3.36. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 180 3. Generate a HU (s) for inbound delivery and execute the goods receipt process in SAP EWM Execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI and follow the header menu path Inbound Delivery • Follow • on Function • Pack. Then, enter the packing material, create an HU, and click Save Delivery. Next, click Goods Receipt, as shown in Figure 3.37. The goods receipt status should now be Completed. Figure 3.36 Display an Inbound Delivery Figure 3.37 Perform Goods Receipt 4. Goods receipt process in SAP EWM triggers an inspection document automatically Execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. sections.title: Pre-Sampling in Production or Inspection after Goods
sections.en: 3.2.2 Pre-Sampling in Production or Inspection after Goods Receipt from Production Pre-sampling for production was first introduced in SAP EWM 9.2. In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for pre-sampling in production. We’ll then walk you step-by-step through a process demo. Business Scenario Pre-sampling is a process utilized for internally produced goods. In SAP EWM, pre-sampling allows inspections to commence prior to the receipt of goods into the warehouse stock from production. This step permits the initiation of a result recording and usage decision at the earliest possible stage. The inspection document can be directly created by releasing the manufacturing order in SAP ERP. Moreover, you can complete a result recording and usage decision even before generating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM. Alternatively, the inspection document can be created while activating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM, and the usage decision can be made before posting the goods receipt. Another choice is to generate the inspection document while activating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM and then making the usage decision before posting the goods receipt. The pre-sampling process after an inbound delivery is shown in Figure 3.46. © 185 Figure 3.46 Pre-Sampling Process for Manufacturing Order Configuration The configuration required for process has one step: setting up the inspection object type. Keep in mind this configuration is just delta configuration in addition to the earlier business process. In this configuration setting, an inspection object type will be set up for pre-sampling goods receipt for production orders. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent IOTS. To create an inspection object type, click New Entries and maintain configuration settings for inspection object type 4 and warehouse 1804. Then, select the Activate IOT checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.47. Also verify that the Prod. Presampling checkbox is activated. Figure 3.47 Pre-Sampling Process for Manufacturing Order Master Data Setup Let’s delve more deeply into the master data required for this process: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 186 1. Inspection rule This master data set up an inspection rule is accessed via the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Quality Management • Maintain Inspection Rule or Transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP. To maintain an inspection rule in SAP EWM, click Create, select the form view, and maintain the Inspection Rule for Inspection process, Product and Inspection type 1704, as shown in Figure 3.48. Figure 3.48 Inspection Rule Setup 2. Inspection plan An inspection plan is utilized to specify the characteristics that must be inspected during each inspection operation and to identify the test equipment that will be utilized for the inspection. Follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Inspection Planning • Create or use Transaction QP01. Maintain the Material and Plan fields and click Continue. Maintain an inspection plan for each combination of product and usage, as shown in Figure 3.49. Figure 3.49 Inspection Plan Process Demo Let’s go step by step through the process for this business scenario: © 187 1. Create a process order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create a process order, execute Transaction COR1. Maintain the Material field and click Continue. On the next screen, Enter the material, storage location, and all the relevant required fields needed to create the process order, as shown in Figure 3.50. Click Save. Note process the order number you’ll need it in the next step. Figure 3.50 Create Process Order 2. Release the process order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To a release process order, execute Transaction COR2. Enter the process order from the previous step and click Continue. Click the Release icon and then click Save. Verify that System Status is REL MSPT PRC BASC, as shown in Figure 3.51. Figure 3.51 Release Process Order 3. Create inbound delivery for process order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create an inbound delivery, execute Transaction MIGO. Enter a process order and click Execute. Click More • Post. Note the inbound delivery, as shown in Figure 3.52, which you’ll need in the next step. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 188 Figure 3.52 Inbound Delivery for Process Order 4. Create HU (s) for an inbound delivery and perform goods receipt in SAP EWM To create HUs and perform goods receipts, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Enter an inbound delivery in the Inbound Delivery field and click Execute. Select a line item on the same screen and, in the header, follow the menu path Inbound Delivery • Follow • On Function • Pack, enter a packing material and create the HU by dragging a product to the HU. Then, click Save to create the HU for the delivery. Now, on the original inbound delivery screen, select the line item and click Goods Receipt, as shown in Figure 3.53. The goods receipt status will be displayed as Completed, and the HU number will appear under the HU tab. To verify the inspection document, on the same screen, click the Document Flow tab, and the inspection document will be displayed with the document category Q01. Note the HU since you’ll need it in the next step. 5. Confirm the putaway warehouse order in SAP EWM To confirm the warehouse order, execute Transaction /SCWM/TO_CONF and input the HU from the previous step into the HU field. Then, select the line item and click Confirm + Save to confirm warehouse order, as shown in Figure 3.54. © 189 Figure 3.53 HU and Production Goods Receipt Figure 3.54 Confirm Warehouse Order 6. Perform a result recording in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To perform a result recording, execute Transaction QE51N. On the initial screen, under the Material tab, enter details into the Material, Batch, and Plant fields and click Execute. On the left side of the screen, select an inspection characteristic and click Accept or Reject. Finally, click Force to perform the result recording, as shown in Figure 3.55. Figure 3.55 Perform Result Recording Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 190 7. Perform a usage decision for the inspection lot in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To perform a usage decision, execute Transaction QA11, Enter the inspection lot and click Execute. The stock item screen will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.56. Input the a decision code into the Decision field, select an action in the Follow Up Actn, field, and select the Trig. Follow-Up checkbox to trigger the follow-up action. Click Save. Figure 3.56 Perform Usage Decision 8. Check the status of the material and the batch and the batch in SAP EWM Once a result recording and a usage decision for the inspection lot is performed successfully, based on the inspection lot result, the material and batch status is changed. To check the status of a material and batch, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Follow the path Stock and Bin • Handling Unit. Input the handling unit in the Handling Unit field and click Execute. The stock status will appear as unrestricted stock F2, as shown in Figure 3.57. Figure 3.57 Display HU Stock Status Note The pre-sampling in production business process with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM is now complete. © 191 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 192

sections.title: Warehouse Stock Inspections
sections.en: 3.3 Warehouse Stock Inspections Internal warehouse inspections involve the examination of inventory within a warehouse and is not directly tied to any inbound or outbound stock processes. The purpose of this inspection is to ensure that inventory levels are accurate, items are in good condition, and the warehouse is operating efficiently. This section will cover stock inspections with inspection rules as well as recurring inspections with inspection rules. Finally, we’ll look at customer return inspections using advanced returns.
sections.he: ‏Internal warehouse inspections — בחינת מלאי בתוך מחסן, לא-קשורה לתהליכי inbound/outbound. מטרה: דיוק רמות מלאי, מצב תקין של פריטים, תפעול יעיל. נכסה stock inspections ו-recurring inspections (עם inspection rules), ולבסוף customer return inspections עם advanced returns.

sections.title: Stock Inspections (With Inspection Rules)
sections.en: 3.3.1 Stock Inspections (With Inspection Rules) Stock inspection involves the examination of inventory either on a recurring basis (for batch-managed products) or on selected stock. To create an internal inspection document for a warehouse, manual creation is required using either a radio frequency (RF) environment or through desktop transactions. In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for internal warehouse stock inspections. We’ll then walk through a process demo step-by-step. Business Scenario Internal warehouse inspection is the process of examining inventory within a warehouse to ensure that the items are in good condition, accurately tracked, and properly stored. This inspection is not associated with any inbound or outbound processes related to stock. These inspections can be conducted on either selected stock or a recurring basis for batch-managed products. To create an internal warehouse inspection document, one must be manually created either an RF environment or desktop transactions. Conducting regular internal warehouse inspections is crucial for ensuring inventory accuracy and efficient warehouse operations. This task enables warehouse personnel to detect and address issues or discrepancies promptly, thus reducing inventory shrinkage, increasing productivity, and enhancing customer satisfaction. © 193 Configuration In this section, we’ll delve into the major configuration steps required for the stock inspection process: 1. Define and activate warehouse-dependent inspection object type in SAP EWM For internal warehouse inspections, object type 5 is the choice. In this case, the inspection planning is performed on the product level. In this configuration setting, a warehouse-dependent inspection object type setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross- Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent IOTs. To define and activate a warehouse-dependent inspection object type, click New Entries. Perform the configuration for inspection object type 5 and select the Activate IOT checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.58. Figure 3.58 Warehouse-Dependent inspection object type settings 2. Generate an inspection object type version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be generated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Generate Inspection Object Types Version. To generate the inspection object type version, select an inspection object type line item (IOT5) and click Generate New Version, as shown in Figure 3.59. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 194 Figure 3.59 Generation of Inspection Object Type Versions 3. Maintain an inspection object type version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Maintain Inspection Object Types Version. To maintain the inspection object type version, select an inspection object type version line item and select the Activ. IOT checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.60. Figure 3.60 Maintain Inspection Object Type Version Note The functionalities of generating an inspection object type version and maintaining an inspection type version do not include the transportation of requests. Therefore, the inspection object type version and inspection type version must be manually configured during the cutover activity of an implementation project. 4. Maintain inspection types in SAP EWM The inspection type determines how an inspection should be carried out. You can define the inspection types and the controls associated with the inspection type. In this configuration setting, inspection types needed for the quality process will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Maintain Inspection Types. Click New Entries and maintain the configuration for the inspection type 1708 and select the One QM Notification per Lot checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.61. © 195 Figure 3.61 Maintain Inspection Types 5. Maintain settings at the plant level in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, plant-dependent quality management settings will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Basic Settings • Maintain Settings at Plant Level. To maintain setting at plant level, select plant line items and click Inspection Type-Specific Settings for Plant. Click New Entries and perform the configuration for inspection type 1708 and plant 1804 (UD Plant), as shown in Figure 3.62. 6. Maintain follow-up actions for quality control in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the follow-up action after quality inspection will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Maintain Follow- Up Actions. Select the Function Modules option from the pane on the left and click New Entries. Maintain function module QFQA_EWM_LOG_FOLLOW_UP_S4, as shown in Figure 3.63. Click Save. Figure 3.62 Inspection Type Specific Settings for Plant Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 196 Figure 3.63 Maintain Follow-Up Action 7. Assign logistical follow-up actions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, logistical follow-up actions will be assigned to the follow-up action. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Define and Activate Warehouse • Maintain Follow-Up Actions • Assign Logistical Follow-Up Actions. Select the line item for the follow-up action and click Assign Logistical Follow-Up Action. Then, maintain the configuration for the combination of warehouse number (1804), follow-up action (EWM_A), and inspection object type (5), as shown in Figure 3.64 for your warehouse. Figure 3.64 Assign Logistical Follow-Up Action Master Data Setup One master data step is required for this process: maintaining the inspection rule in SAP EWM. Maintain the inspection rule via SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse © 197 Management • Master Data • Quality Management • Maintain Inspection Rule or use Transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP. To maintain an inspection rule in SAP EWM, click Create, select the Form view, and maintain the inspection rule for inspection type 1708, as shown in Figure 3.65. Figure 3.65 Maintain Inspection Rule Process Demo Let’s go through the process for this business scenario step by step: 1. Create an inspection lot in SAP EWM To create an inspection lot, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Follow the path Stock and Bin • Physical Path and then double-click Physical Path. Enter the product and batch and click Execute. Select line item and select the option More Methods • Create Insp (IOT5). In the popup window that appears, enter exception code CRID and execute the transaction, as shown in Figure 3.66. Figure 3.66 Create Inspection Lot 2. Display an inspection lot in the warehouse monitor in the warehouse monitor in SAP EWM To display an inspection lot, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Follow the path Document • Inspection. Double-click Inspection and enter the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 198 inspection lot from the previous step. The inspection lot will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.67. Figure 3.67 Display Inspection Lot in Warehouse Monitor 3. Record usage decisions in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To record a usage decision, execute Transaction QA11. Enter the inspection lot from earlier and click Execute. The stock item screen will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.68. Click Mass Inspection for Selected Items. Then, maintain the Decision and Follow-Up Actn field and select the Trig. Follow-Up checkbox to trigger the follow-up action. Click Save. Figure 3.68 Record Usage Decision 4. Display an inspection lot in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display an inspection lot, execute Transaction QA03, input the inspection lot number into the Inspection Lot field and then click Continue. On the next screen, the inspection lot will be displayed. Note the values in the Insp. Lot. Orig (inspection lot origin) and Inspection Type fields, as shown in Figure 3.69. © 199 Figure 3.69 Display Inspection Lot 5. Display a material document in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display a material document, execute Transaction MB51; enter material, batch, and plant values and click Execute. On the next screen, the material document will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.70. Figure 3.70 Display Material Document in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA 6. Display stock in SAP EWM To display stock, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON and follow the path Stock and Bin • Available Stock. Double-click Available Stock; then input the product and batch and click Execute. The stock will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.71. Note the stock type is marked as Unrestricted. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 200 Figure 3.71 Display Stock in SAP EWM Note The process for internal warehouse stock inspections with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM is now complete.

sections.title: Recurring Inspections (With Inspection Rules)
sections.en: 3.3.2 Recurring Inspections (With Inspection Rules) Some industries, such as chemicals and pharmaceuticals, require regular inspections of batch-managed products in the warehouse. A recurring inspection is a type of warehouse-internal inspection that is not related to inbound or outbound processes, but rather to internal warehouse processes. Recurring inspections are essential for batch-managed products, but they can also be performed for any product that requires periodic inspection. To carry out recurring inspections, inspection object type 5 (Q-Inspection Product/Batch Warehouse Internal) is used. In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for recurring internal stock inspections. Business Scenario As shown in Figure 3.72, the system can determine the date of next inspection for a batch-managed product via the Inspection Interval feature. To use this feature, you must first assign a class that includes the standard characteristic LOBM_QNDAT (next inspection date) to the batch. © 201 Figure 3.72 Recurring Inspection When a new batch is created, the system automatically assigns the next inspection date by following these conditions: If the manufacturing date is available for the batch, the system calculates the next inspection date by adding the inspection interval (which is maintained in the material/product master) to the manufacturing date. If the manufacturing date is NOT available for the batch, the system calculates the next inspection date by adding the inspection interval (which is maintained in the material/product master) to the batch creation date. Configuration In this section, we’ll delve into the major configuration required for the stock inspection process: 1. Define and activate warehouse-dependent inspection object types in SAP EWM For the warehouse internal inspections object type 5 is the choice. In this case, the inspection planning is performed on the product level. In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be generated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 202 Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Maintain Inspection Object Types Version. To define and activate warehouse-dependent inspection object types, click New Entries and perform the configuration for the warehouse number for inspection object type 5, as shown in Figure 3.73. Figure 3.73 Maintain and Activate Inspection Type Version 2. Generate an inspection object type version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be generated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Generate Inspection Object Types Version. To generate the inspection object type, select the inspection object type line item for inspection object type 5 and click Generate New Version, as shown in Figure 3.74. Figure 3.74 Generation of Inspection Object Type Version © 203 3. Maintain an inspection object type version in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, an inspection object type version will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Basics and Integration • Maintain Inspection Object Types Version. Select the inspection object type version line item and select the Activ. IOT checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.75. 4. Maintain inspection types in SAP EWM The inspection type determines how an inspection should be carried out. You can define the inspection types and the controls associated with the inspection type. In this configuration setting, inspection types needed for the quality process will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Maintain Inspection Types. Click New Entries and maintain the configuration for the inspection type 1709 and select the One QM Notification per Lot checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.76. Figure 3.75 Maintain Inspection Object Type Version Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 204 Figure 3.76 Maintain Inspection Types 5. Define default values for the inspection type in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, inspection types needed for quality process will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Define Default Values for Inspection Type. Click New Entries, maintain the configuration for inspection type 1709, and select the Inspect by Task List checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.77. Figure 3.77 Define Default Value for the Inspection Type 6. Maintain settings at the plant level in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, plant-dependent quality management settings © 205 will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Basic Settings • Maintain Settings at Plant Level. Then, select plant line items and click Inspection Type-Specific Settings for Plant. Click New Entries. Perform the configuration for inspection type 1701 and plant 1804 (UD Plant), as shown in Figure 3.78. Figure 3.78 Inspection Type Setting for Plant 7. Maintain follow-up actions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, follow up action after quality inspection will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path: SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Maintain Follow- Up Actions. Click New Entries and maintain configuration setting for function module QFQA_EWM_LOG _FOLLOW_UP_S4, as shown in Figure 3.79. Click Save. Figure 3.79 Follow-Up Action Function Module 8. Assign logistical follow-up actions in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, a logistical follow-up action will be assigned. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Quality Management • Inspection Results • Define and Activate Warehouse • Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 206 Maintain Follow-Up Actions • Assign Logistical Follow-up Actions. Select the line item that requires a follow-up action assignment and click Assign Logistical Follow-Up Actions on the left. Then, for your warehouse, maintain the configuration for Then, maintain the configuration for the combination of warehouse number (1804), follow-up action (EWM_A), and inspection object type (5), as shown in Figure 3.80. 9. Define exception codes in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, exception codes for inspection lots will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Settings • Exception Handling • Define Exception Codes. Click New Entries and create exception code CRID for the warehouse, as shown in Figure 3.81. Click Save. Figure 3.80 Assign Logistical Follow-Up Action Figure 3.81 Define Exception Code Master Data Setup Let’s delve into the master data required for process step by step: © 207 1. Define inspection rules in SAP EWM This master data set up is to maintain inspection rule using SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Quality Management • Maintain Inspection Rule or Transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP. Click Create, select the Form view of the screen, and maintain the Inspection Rule for Inspection type 1709, as shown in Figure 3.82. Figure 3.82 Define Inspection Rule 2. Material master: maintain inspection interval in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA This master data setting will be used for maintain material master using SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • Material Management • Material Master • Material • Create (General) or via Transaction MM01. Maintain the Material, Industry section, and material type and click continue. Select the Quality management view and maintain the Inspection Interval field as 3 days, as shown in Figure 3.83. Figure 3.83 Material Master 3. Assign batch characteristics to class in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA This master data setting assigns batch characteristics to a class. Follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Cross-Application Components • Classification System • Master Data • Classes or execute Transaction CL02. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 208 Maintain the Class and Class type fields and click the Change icon (pencil). Select the Char. tab and assign characteristics to the class, as shown in Figure 3.84. Click Save. Figure 3.84 Display Class 4. Display batch in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA This master data setup will be used to display the batch. Follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • Material Management • Material Master • Material • Create (General) or execute Transaction MSC3N. Enter a material, batch, plant, and storage location. The batch will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.85. Figure 3.85 Display Batch Process Demo Let’s go through the process for this business scenario step by step: © 209 1. Create inspection lot in SAP EWM To create inspection lot, execute Transaction /SCWM/STOCK_ATT_CHG. Select the option Create Insp. And Post Stock to QM stock, enter material, batch, exception code-CRID and all the details such as Product and Batch and click Execute button on the same screen as shown in Figure 3.86 and click Execute. Figure 3.86 Create Inspection Lot 2. Check the inspection lot for material and batch in SAP EWM To check inspection lot, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Follow the path Document • Inspection. Double-click Inspection. Enter the inspection lot from the previous step. The inspection lot will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.87. Figure 3.87 Display the Inspection Lot 3. Perform the usage decision for the inspection lot in SAP EWM To perform the usage decision, execute Transaction QA11, Enter the inspection lot from the previous step and click Execute. The stock item screen will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.88. Click Mass Inspection for Selected Items, maintain the Decision and Follow-Up Actn fields, and select the Trig. Follow-Up checkbox. Click Save. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 210 Figure 3.88 Perform Usage Decision 4. Verify the next inspection date on the batch in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To verify the next inspection date, execute Transaction MSC3N. Maintain the Material and Batch fields and press (Enter) and check the date in the Next Inspection field, as shown in Figure 3.89. Figure 3.89 Display Batch Next Inspection Note The recurring inspection business process with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM is now complete.
