sections.title: Customer Return Inspections Using Advanced Returns
sections.en: 3.3.3 Customer Return Inspections Using Advanced Returns Management SAP has offered advanced returns management in embedded EWM since the release of SAP S/4HANA 1709. Previously, most clients utilized the advanced returns management process for customer returns, which involved connecting © 211 quality inspections, manually generating free-of-charge sales orders to send replacement material, and verifying the availability of that material via multiple transactions Additionally, creating credit memos for refunds and manually adjusting the price based on the quality inspection results were necessary. However, all of these manual tasks can be streamlined through advanced returns management, which is a powerful tool for all reverse logistics. Advanced returns management can capture almost all complex return processes with minimal effort. Business Scenario As shown in Figure 3.90, you can effectively manage customer returns through the utilization of SAP ERP’s advanced returns management feature. This exceptional functionality seamlessly integrates with SAP EWM, so you can efficiently handle returned items at the granular level of storage bins. Figure 3.90 Customer Return Process in Advanced Returns Management This remarkable quality management component of SAP EWM means you can conduct meticulous inspections on returned items, thereby significantly enhancing the efficiency and transparency of the entire process. To initiate the returns process, you can create either an advanced returns management returns order or a returns stock transport order. Consequently, you’re presented with two distinct options for conducting comprehensive quality inspections: Option 1: Performing the inspection prior to the goods being received in the SAP ERP system via advanced returns management Option 1 entails carrying out the inspection, making a decision, and performing subsequent logistical actions entirely within the SAP ERP system. If a follow-on document for a logistical action is generated in SAP ERP, the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 212 external inspection ID is transmitted to SAP EWM alongside the delivery document. This crucial information is then stored with the corresponding stock item, facilitating the accurate determination of the stock item for the follow-on document, which is subsequently replicated from SAP ERP. Option 2: Performingthe inspection during the goods receipt process by leveraging the capabilities of SAP EWM or the Quality Inspection Engine With Option 2, the return items undergo a meticulous inspection within SAP EWM as soon as they arrive at the goods receipt area or designated work centers. Simple logistical actions, such as putaway or scrapping, can be conveniently performed directly within SAP EWM. However, for more intricate follow-up actions, the responsibility can be seamlessly transferred to SAP ERP. The processing of follow-on documents created in SAP ERP is conclusively executed within SAP EWM, effectively finalizing the comprehensive inspection process. Within this section, our primary focus will be on Option 2. This approach involves conducting the inspection during the goods receipt process by leveraging the robust capabilities of SAP EWM or the sophisticated functions of the Quality Inspection Engine. Configuration In this section, we’ll delve into the major configuration steps required for advanced returns management: 1. Activate advanced returns management for the return order type in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA In this configuration setting, return order type will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path Sales and Distribution • Sales • Advanced Returns Management • Activate Advanced Return Management for Return Order Types. Select the sales document RE2 in the Sales Doc. Type field and select the Adv. Return checkbox, as shown in Figure 3.91. © 213 Figure 3.91 Activate Advanced Returns Management 2. Activate and rename follow-up activities in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA In this configuration setting, the return order type will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path Sales and Distribution • Sales • Advanced Returns Management • Activate and Rename Follow-Up Activities. To activate and rename follow up activities, on this screen, verify the activity description, as shown in Figure 3.92, If you want to change any activity description according to your business processes, you can do so in the Activity Description column. Figure 3.92 Activate and Rename Follow-Up Activities 3. Activate business configuration (BC) sets for advanced returns management in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the BC set will be activated. Follow the IMG menu path Tools • Customizing • Business Configuration Sets • Activation of BC Sets. Click the Activate button and activate the following BC sets one by one, as shown in Figure 3.93: /SCWM/DLV_INBOUND_RETURN Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 214 /SCWM/DLV_TRANSFER_ARM_TYPE /SCWM/DLV_OUTBOUND_BACK_CUST Figure 3.93 Activate BC Sets 4. Edit code groups and codes for usage decisions in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA In this configuration setting, you will define code groups and codes. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot completion • Edit Code Groups and Usage Decisions. Click New Entries and maintain the Code Group and codes 0001, 0002, 0003, and 0004, as shown in Figure 3.94. Figure 3.94 Code for Usage Decision 5. Edit selected sets for usage decisions for usage decisions in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA In this configuration setting, you can edit selected sets for usage decisions. Follow the IMG menu path Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Completion • Edit Selected Sets for Usage Decisions. Maintain the Plant and Selected Set fields and then define sets via the Code Group and Code fields, as shown in Figure 3.95. © 215 Figure 3.95 Selected Set Codes for Usage Decision 6. Configuring the document type for inbound delivery in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the document type for advanced returns management with inbound deliveries will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Inbound Delivery • Define Document Types for Inbound Delivery. Click New Entries. Then, in the Document Type field, enter “IRET” and enter “PDI” in the Doc. Categ. field, as shown in Figure 3.96. Click Save. Figure 3.96 Define Inbound Delivery Document Type 7. Configuring item type for inbound delivery in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the item type for advanced returns management with inbound deliveries will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Inbound Delivery • Define Item Types for Inbound Delivery. Click New Entries. Then, in the Document Type field, enter “IRET” and enter “PDI” in the Doc. Categ. field, as shown in Figure 3.97. Click Save. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 216 Figure 3.97 Define Item Type for Inbound Delivery 8. Define the allowed document type and item types and item types for inbound delivery in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the document type and item type will be mapped. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Inbound Delivery • Define Item Types for Inbound Delivery. Click New Entries. Then, in the Document Type field, enter “IRET” and enter “IRET” in the Item Type field, as shown in Figure 3.98. Click Save. 9. Define ERP document type for differentiation attributes in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the document type and item type will be mapped. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Define ERP Document Types for Differentiation Attribute. Click New Entries and maintain DocTypeERP and Profile, as shown in Figure 3.99. © 217 Figure 3.98 Allowed Item Type and Document Type Figure 3.99 ERP Document Type for Differentiate Attribute 10. Configure mapping of document types in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the document type will be mapped. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Document Type from ERP system to EWM. Click New Entries and maintain Doc.Type ERP and Document Type EWM, as shown in Figure 3.100. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 218 Figure 3.100 Map Document Type ERP and Document Type EWM 11. Configure mapping of item types in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, the item type will be mapped. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Item Type from ERP system to EWM. Click New Entries and maintain Item Type ERP REN2and Document Type ERP LR2, as shown in Figure 3.101. Click Save. Figure 3.101 Map Item Type ERP and Item Type EWM 12. Configure mapping of date types in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, date type will be mapped. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • ERP Integration • Delivery Processing • Map Date Types from ERP System to EWM. Click New Entries. Then, maintain DType ERP and Document type IRET and provide start and end dates, as shown in Figure 3.102. Click Save. © 219 Figure 3.102 Mapping of Date Types 13. Define a warehouse process type for return advanced returns management in SAP EWM In this configuration setting, a warehouse process type will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Setting • Warehouse Task • Define Warehouse Process Type. Click New Entries and maintain configuration for warehouse process type 4030 with activity PTWY as shown in Figure 3.103. Click Save. Figure 3.103 Define Warehouse Process Type 14. Determine warehouse process type for return advanced returns management In this configuration setting, the warehouse process type will be determined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Cross-Process Setting • Warehouse Task • Determine Warehouse Process Type. Click New Entries and maintain warehouse process type 4030 and document type IRET (Doc. Type), as shown in Figure 3.104. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 220 Figure 3.104 Determine Warehouse Process Type Process Demo Let’s go through the process for this advanced returns management business scenario step by step: 1. Create a return customer sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create a sales order, execute Transaction VA01. Enter order type RE2 and Sales Area details. Click Continue and enter sales order details, such as the material and quantity, and click Save to create return sales order, as shown in Figure 3.105. Note the sales order number, which you’ll need for the next step. 2. Display an advanced returns delivery in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display an advanced returns delivery, execute Transaction VA03. On the first screen, input the sales order number from the previous step and click Continue. On the next screen, which displays the sales order, select a line item and click the Display Document Flow icon; you’ll see the outbound delivery number alone with the sales order number. Select an outbound delivery line item and click Display Document, and the delivery (a return outbound delivery) will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.106. © 221 Figure 3.105 Create Return Sales Order Figure 3.106 Display Returns Delivery 3. Display the inbound delivery in SAP EWM To display the inbound delivery, execute Transaction SCWM/PRDI. Input the inbound delivery from the previous step and click Execute. The inbound delivery will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.107. 4. Perform the goods receipt for the inbound delivery in SAP EWM To perform the goods receipt, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Enter the inbound delivery into the Inbound Delivery field. Click Goods Receipt, and the goods receipt status will be updated to Completed, as shown in Figure 3.108. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 222 Figure 3.107 Display Inbound Delivery in SAP EWM Figure 3.108 Goods Receipt for Inbound Delivery 5. Goods receipt for inbound delivery triggers an RMA in SAP EWM To display a return material authorization, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Input the inbound delivery into Inbound Delivery field and click Perform Search. The RMA is displayed, as shown in Figure 3.109. Note the inbound delivery number as you’ll need it in the next step. 6. Perform a material inspection in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To perform a material inspection, execute Transaction MSR_INSPWH, input the Inbound Delivery in the Delivery field, and click Execute. On the next screen, enter the follow-up action and click Save and Confirm, as shown in Figure 3.110. © 223 Figure 3.109 Display Return Material Authorization Figure 3.110 Perform Material Inspection 7. Display the material inspection in the warehouse in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display the material inspection, execute Transaction MSR_INSPWH, enter the inbound delivery from the previous step into the Delivery field, and click Execute. The material inspection will be displayed, as shown in Figure 3.111. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 224 Figure 3.111 Display Material Inspection 8. Display the document flow for the customer sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display the sales order, execute Transaction VA03. On the initial screen, input a sales order number and click Continue. On the next screen, select a line item and click Display Document. The next screen will display the document flow’s details, as shown in Figure 3.112. Figure 3.112 Display Document Flow for Return Order 9. Display a stock overview for the material in SAP EWM To display the stock overview, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Follow the path Stock and Bin • Handling Unit and double-click Handling Unit. Enter the HU into HU field and click Execute. The stock is blocked with stock type B6, as shown in Figure 3.113. © 225 Figure 3.113 Display Stock Overview Note The advanced returns management business process with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM is now complete. sections.he:
‏SAP מציעה advanced returns management ב-embedded EWM מאז SAP S/4HANA 1709. קודם לכן, customer returns כללו חיבור ידני של inspections, יצירת free-of-charge sales orders, בדיקת זמינות, וניהול credit memos ידני. ‏advanced returns management מייעל את כל reverse logistics בקלות.

**תרחיש עסקי** (Figure 3.90) — ניהול customer returns דרך advanced returns management של SAP ERP, המשתלב עם SAP EWM לטיפול ברמת ה-storage bin. ליזום: ‏advanced returns management returns order או returns stock transport order. שתי אפשרויות ל-inspection:
• **Option 1** — inspection, decision, ו-logistical actions כולן ב-SAP ERP. אם נוצר follow-on document, ה-external inspection ID מועבר ל-SAP EWM עם ה-delivery document.
• **Option 2** — ה-return items עוברים inspection ב-SAP EWM עם הגעתם לאזור ה-GR או work centers. פעולות פשוטות (putaway/scrapping) ב-SAP EWM; ל-follow-up מורכב, האחריות מועברת ל-SAP ERP.

נתמקד ב-Option 2.

**Configuration:**
1. **Activate ARM for return order type** — Sales and Distribution • Sales • Advanced Returns Management • Activate Advanced Return Management for Return Order Types. ‏Sales Doc. Type RE2, ‏Adv. Return (Figure 3.91).

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 3.5 Summary Our chapter on quality management is now complete. In this chapter, we explored various aspects of quality management, starting with an overview of the quality management process in SAP EWM. Additionally, we covered the inspection of goods received from external vendors and the pre-sampling procedures involved in the goods receipt process. Furthermore, you learned about two kinds of internal stock inspection processes, namely, ad-hoc inspections and recurring stock inspections, which are commonly utilized in internal warehouse inspections. Finally, we explored the advanced customer returns management process. By delving into these topics, you now have a comprehensive understanding of quality management and its various facets. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 228 4 Transportation Management SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) is an innovative software solution that empowers enterprises to strategically orchestrate the movement of goods and materials within their supply chains. This cutting- edge program affords organizations invaluable real-time visibility into transportation operations, enabling them to adroitly optimize logistics processes, curtail costs, and bolster customer service. The program’s robust features facilitate the agile planning and booking of freight, the expeditious management of carriers, the seamless tracking and visibility of shipments, and intuitive analytics and reporting capabilities. The objective of this chapter is to provide you with a complete guide to integrating SAP TM with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM). To accomplish this goal, we’ll offer an exhaustive exposition of the business processes linked to each technique, followed by an elaborate examination of the configuration and master data prerequisites crucial to facilitate end- to-end testing of your business scenarios. Ultimately, we’ll provide step-by- step demonstrations of each process to further solidify your comprehension. SAP EWM can be seamlessly integrated with SAP TM to optimize logistics operations and bolster supply chain visibility. This integration engenders a harmonized platform for end-to-end logistics management, thereby streamlining transportation planning and execution, while also facilitating efficient warehouse operations. By integrating SAP EWM with SAP TM, businesses can reap a multitude of advantages and benefits. These benefits include enhanced transportation planning and execution, real-time visibility into shipment and delivery status, improved inventory accuracy and control, and augmented productivity through automation and streamlined processes. Additionally, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP TM culminates in a centralized data repository for logistics information, thereby enabling better decision- making and analysis. This chapter provides a thorough exploration of the most up-to-date business processes within SAP EWM and SAP TM. We cover advanced shipping and ©

sections.title: Overview of Transportation Management
sections.en: 4.1 Overview of Transportation Management Systems A transportation management system is a software platform that the transportation industry employs to plan, execute, and optimize the movements of goods, including both inbound and outbound shipments. A transportation management system ensures compliance with regulations and furnishes the necessary documentation. Managing transportation can be complex, expensive, and time consuming, and thus, a transportation management system is a crucial tool for streamlining supply chains. Transportation was once viewed as a distinct business process, but now it is integrated into overall supply chain and logistics management. A transportation management system frequently forms part of a larger supply chain management system. To deal with the growing complexity and uncertainty of global logistics, businesses must improve logistics processes, enhance services, and increase visibility and control. A transportation management system provides a holistic perspective of daily transportation operations, encompassing trade compliance data, essential documentation, and the timely delivery of goods and freight. Transportation Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 230 management system solutions streamline shipping processes, allowing an enterprise to oversee and enhance its transportation operations across various modes of transportation, such as land, air, and sea. Transportation management systems play a crucial role in modern supply chains, affecting each stage of the process, from planning and procurement to logistics and lifecycle management. A strong transportation management system offers comprehensive visibility, facilitating more effective transportation planning and execution, leading to improved customer satisfaction and increased sales growth. Given the continuously changing global trade environment, having a transportation management system that can assist businesses in successfully navigating complex trade policies and guaranteeing compliance with regulations is vital. Transportation management systems are primarily employed by businesses that require frequent shipping, moving, and receiving services, such as manufacturers, distributors, e-commerce companies, and retail businesses. Additionally, logistics service providers, including third-party logistics (3PL) and fourth-party logistics (4PL) firms, commonly use transportation management systems to provide logistics services to their clients. The SAP TM application integrates fleet management and logistics management, streamlining the movement of goods across various modes of transportation. In this way, SAP TM enhances operational efficiency and reduces costs. This solution offers a range of features, including transportation demand management, order consolidation, shipment monitoring and tracking, and transportation spend optimization. Additionally, it facilitates strategic freight procurement, capacity monitoring, freight order management, and transportation planning optimization. Furthermore, SAP TM assists in the management of freight financials through freight settlement and provides analysis and reporting capabilities to make informed transportation decisions. Employing SAP TM, enterprises can implement a uniform transportation system that results in decreased transportation expenses and increased customer contentment. This software streamlines transportation planning, execution, and cost reconciliation, while also furnishing valuable data analytics to augment the overall transportation process. As shown in Figure 4.1, SAP TM, when used in conjunction with SAP S/4HANA, can be deployed in a variety of deployment and integration scenarios. © 231 Figure 4.1 SAP TM Deployment Options The following list describes these options in more detail: Internal system or embedded integration In this first scenario, referred to as internal system integration or embedded integration, SAP TM is directly integrated into the SAP S/4HANA system instance. In this approach, SAP TM can directly access logistics data within the SAP S/4HANA system, thus eliminating the need for data transfers between the systems. This approach eliminates the possibility of redundant data and reduces the effort required for data transfer. External system or side-by-side integration In this second scenario, referred to as external system integration or side-by- side integration, SAP TM is implemented as a separate system. In this approach, master data and transactional data are transmitted from the SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP system to SAP TM using various techniques for replicating master data. SAP TM, which is a component of SAP S/4HANA, can function as a standalone system in side-by-side scenarios in the following ways: SAP TM can be integrated with existing enterprise resource planning (ERP) instances that have not yet been converted to SAP S/4HANA, as part of the SAP S/4HANA system. In situations with multiple SAP S/4HANA instances in a system landscape, SAP TM can be integrated with each instance. SAP TM can be implemented with support packs and released independently of other SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management applications Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 232 to accommodate different software lifecycle management requirements. While this option may result in a higher total cost of ownership (TCO), the trade-off might be necessary. Note Note that, for additional information on deployment and integration options, we recommend consulting the following SAP Notes: 2714892 - SAP Transportation Management - Deployment Options 2812981 - Transportation Management and decentralized EWM in same SAP S/4HANA system and client Integration options between SAP EWM and SAP TM Different integration options between SAP EWM and SAP TM are available, such as the following: Direct integration of embedded EWM and embedded SAP TM on SAP S/4HANA As shown in Figure 4.2, the SAP S/4HANA platform presents a seamless fusion of embedded EWM and embedded SAP TM modules. This amalgamation facilitates instantaneous communications between the two modules and enables a comprehensive look at logistics operations. By virtue of this direct integration, SAP EWM and SAP TM leverage a unified database, effectively eliminating data redundancy and ensuring data coherence. Figure 4.2 Direct Integration of Embedded EWM and Embedded SAP TM Integrate decentralized Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (decentralized EWM) and standalone SAP TM As shown in Figure 4.3, SAP S/4HANA provides a streamlined solution for integrating your decentralized EWM and standalone SAP TM modules. This © 233 approach allows for enhanced supply chain management capabilities, enabling your organization to efficiently oversee the flow of goods and optimize logistics processes. Figure 4.3 Integrate Decentralized EWM and Standalone SAP TM Integrate decentralized EWM on SAP S/4HANA and embedded SAP TM on SAP S/4HANA and embedded SAP TM on SAP S/4HANA As shown in Figure 4.4, SAP S/4HANA provides seamless integration between a decentralized EWM system and the embedded SAP TM modules. Figure 4.4 Integrate Decentralized EWM and Embedded SAP TM Indirectly integrate SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA As shown in Figure 4.5, in this particular scenario, the SAP EWM and SAP TM systems can be integrated with SAP ERP, and the exchange of data between these systems is facilitated through the SAP ERP system. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 234 Figure 4.5 Indirect Integration SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP Several benefits of this indirect integration approach include the following: Leveraging existing SAP ERP infrastructure and investments: By integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP, a business can make the most of its existing infrastructure and investment in SAP ERP systems. This approach can reduce the cost and effort required to deploy and maintain separate systems for warehouse management and transportation management. Streamlined data flow between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and other ERP modules: Indirect integration between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and other ERP modules, such as sales, procurement, and inventory management, can help streamline data flows across different business functions. This approach can lead to improved data accuracy, better decision-making, and reduced errors. Improved visibility and control over end-to-end supply chain processes: By integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP, a business can gain better visibility and control over its supply chain processes. This approach can help identify and address issues quickly, optimize operations, and improve customer satisfaction. Management of transportation planning and execution within the context of broader business processes: Integrating SAP EWM and SAP TM with SAP ERP can help a business manage transportation planning and execution within the context of broader business processes, such as order fulfillment and inventory management. This approach can help ensure that transportation plans are aligned with broader business goals and objectives. © 235 Reduced manual effort and increased efficiency through automation: Indirect integration between SAP EWM, SAP TM, and SAP ERP can help reduce manual effort and increase efficiency through automation. This approach can lead to faster processing times, reduced errors, and improved productivity. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 236

sections.en: 4.2 Shipping and Receiving in Inbound and Outbound Processes Shipping and receiving in inbound and outbound processes in SAP EWM are essential components of warehouse management systems. SAP EWM streamlines shipping and receiving processes, providing real-time visibility, efficient order processing, and enhanced inventory control. By automating and optimizing these processes, a business can improve in overall warehouse efficiency, can reduce errors, and can enhance customer satisfaction. SAP provides a range of business processes aimed at facilitating seamless integration between transportation management processes and warehouse management processes, with the ultimate goal of meeting customer requirements. These processes are designed to ensure the smooth management of inbound and outbound shipments, as well as the efficient use of transportation units (TUs) and vehicles within a warehouse. The shipping and receiving aspects of EWM encompass the following key areas: Utilization of vehicles and TUs to manage goods transport to and from the warehouse Loading and unloading operations, including docking and undocking procedures at warehouse doors Yard management, which involves the organization and optimization of warehouse yard space Regarding inbound and outbound processes, shipping and receiving processes play a vital role in efficiently planning and executing warehouse activities. By leveraging these processes, your business can effectively manage the flow of goods, handle incoming shipments, and ensure timely and accurate deliveries to customers or other destinations. The integration of shipping and receiving functionalities in both inbound and outbound operations enhances overall warehouse efficiency, inventory control, and customer satisfaction as well as enable the following capabilities: Integration of freight orders in SAP TM (processes based on freight order integration in SAP TM) © 237 This process involves linking SAP TM with SAP EWM to manage inbound and outbound shipments. Use of vehicles and TUs and TUs in SAP EWM (processes based on use of vehicles and TUs in SAP EWM) This process entails integrating SAP EWM with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to manage TUs and vehicles within the warehouse. Shipment integration in SAP ERP (processes based on use of shipment integration in SAP ERP) This process involves connecting SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA with SAP EWM to oversee shipments and related processes. Shipment integration in SAP ERP and SAP TM (processes based on use of shipment and integration in SAP ERP and SAP TM) This process involves integrating SAP TM and SAP EWM with SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to oversee shipments throughout the transportation and warehouse management process as a whole. In summary, SAP offers various business processes that support the integration of transportation management and warehouse management processes to enable a seamless experience for users and customers. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 238

sections.title: Freight Order Integration
sections.en: 4.3 Freight Order Integration For inbound goods receipts as well as outbound goods issues, transportation planning is performed in SAP TM based on purchase orders, deliveries, sales orders, or customer return orders in SAP ERP. SAP TM sends planned freight order data directly to SAP EWM, which converts the information from the freight order into planned shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM, namely, activities involving vehicles or TUs. You can perform all warehouse activities, such as loading or unloading, and perform goods receipts or goods issues for all deliveries.

sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.en: 4.3.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll go through the inbound goods receipt process using freight order integration in SAP TM. We’ll explore transportation planning based on purchase orders in the following sections. Business Process Figure 4.6 shows the step-by-step process for inbound goods receipt, which is performed in the following sequence: 1. Purchase orders are received by SAP TM from either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, and their corresponding transportation requirements and freight units are generated. 2. Transportation planning is carried out based on transportation requirements, and freight orders are created in SAP TM. 3. If transportation planning is based on purchase orders, SAP TM generates deliveries in either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 4. Inbound deliveries are then distributed by SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP EWM, which automatically generates corresponding warehouse requests. 5. Freight order information is sent by SAP TM to SAP EWM, which automatically creates planned shipping and receiving activities for the assigned vehicle or TU. Inbound deliveries are also assigned to the created TU activities. © 239 6. The system automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active when a warehouse operator or checkpoint clerk executes the arrival at checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU. 7. An operator or goods receipt clerk then assigns a door to the vehicle or TU. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door; if not, the Arrival at Door action is executed for the vehicle or TU. 8. Warehouse activities, such as unloading goods, posting goods receipts, and putting away goods, are then carried out. 9. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard; if not, the Departure from Door action is executed for the vehicle or TU. 10. The operator executes the Departure from Checkpoint action for the vehicle or TUs, and SAP EWM automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Active to Completed. This action triggers a notification to SAP TM about the executed shipping and receiving activities for the vehicle or TU, and the freight order is updated accordingly. 11. The SAP TM freight order’s execution status is then set to Completed. 12. Freight settlement is carried out in SAP TM, and the freight settlement document serves as the basis for invoice verification and settlement in SAP ERP. Figure 4.6 Freight Order Integration in SAP TM and SAP EWM: Inbound Process Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 240 Configuration In this section, we’ll explore the key configuration steps needed for this process, assuming that the primary SAP EWM customization settings are already configured in the system: 1. Define control keys for document integration You define control keys that specify which documents in a document chain are to be integrated into SAP TM. You can define as many control keys as required, with different combinations of relevant documents. In this setting, a control key for document integration will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Integration with Other SAP Components • Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Define Control Key for Document Integration. To define a control key for document integration, click New Entries and maintain control key parameters. If you’re using order-based planning, make sure the PO to TM checkbox is activated, as shown in Figure 4.7. Figure 4.7 Control Key Parameters 2. Define a logistic integration profile You can control settings for the building of freight units when working with the internal SAP TM component. You can create and assign profiles to SAP TM-relevant business document types. In this setting, a logistics integration profile and corresponding freight order building rule will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Internal TM Component Integration • Define Logistics Integration Profile. To define logistic integration profiles, click New Entries and configure logistics integration profile Y002 and maintain other details, as shown in Figure 4.8. Alternatively, you can verify that standard SAP configuration settings on this screen meet your business requirements. © 241 3. Define the transport-relevance of purchasing documents You can activate the integration of purchase orders into SAP TM by assigning a control key to the required purchase order. In this setting, transport-relevant purchasing document setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Internal TM Component Integration • Define Transportation-Relevance of Purchasing Documents. To define transportation-relevant purchasing documents, click New Entries and configure transport-relevant purchasing document settings for control key 0055 and with logistics integration profile Y002 (Log Int. Profile) as shown in Figure 4.9. Alternatively, you can verify that standard SAP configuration settings on this screen meet your business requirements.. Figure 4.8 Logistics Integration Profile Figure 4.9 Transport-Relevant Purchasing Document 4. Define the transport relevance of delivery documents You activate the integration of inbound deliveries into SAP TM by assigning a control key to the required inbound delivery. In this setting, the transport- relevant delivery document setting will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Logistics Integration • Internal TM Component Integration • Define Transportation-Relevance of Delivery Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 242 Documents. Click New Entries and configure transport-relevant delivery document settings for control key 0056 (Control Key), logistics integration profile Y002 (Log. Int. Profile), and delivery type EL (Del. Type), as shown in Figure 4.10. Alternatively, you can verify that standard SAP configuration settings on this screen meet your business requirements. Figure 4.10 Transport-Relevant Delivery Document 5. Create a freight unit building rule In this SAP NetWeaver setting, a freight unit building rule will be defined. Follow the SAP NetWeaver menu path Application • Administration • Planning • General Planning Settings • Freight Unit Building Rule • Create Freight Unit Building Rule. As shown in Figure 4.11, verify that Document Type 0001 has been maintained and the value in the Critical Quantity field is Gross Weight. 6. Define freight order types Freight orders are created as the result of planning, especially in land transportation, and the freight bookings are used in air or sea transportation. In a subcontracting process, a freight order is the transportation document that is sent to the carrier once assigned via carrier selection or tendering. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Freight Order Management • Freight Order • Define Freight Order Types. To define a freight order type, click New Entries and configure freight order settings, as shown in Figure 4.12. Enter “2000” into the EWM Integration Profile field and “1000” into the Freight Order Type field. © 243 Figure 4.11 Display Freight Unit Building Rule Figure 4.12 Freight Order Type 7. Define an SAP EWM integration profile You can define a profile for direct integration with SAP EWM or an external warehouse management system. In this setting, SAP EWM integration profile will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path Transportation Management • Integration • Integration with Extended Warehouse Management • Define EWM Integration Profile. Click New Entries and maintain the SAP EWM integration profile, as shown Figure 4.13. Verify the sending loading and unloading instructions in the Settings for Inbound and Settings for Outbound Stop. To activate messages in the PPF, select the Action Definition checkboxes for the lines highlighted in the table shown in in Figure 4.14. Figure 4.21 SAP TM: Display Inbound Delivery 6. Display the inbound delivery in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To display the inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL33N. Enter the inbound delivery in the Inbound Delivery field from the previous step and click Continue. The inbound delivery is shown in Figure 4.22. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 248 7. Display unloading instructions in SAP TM The SAP TM system sends unloading instructions to SAP EWM. To display these unloading instructions, execute the SAP Fiori app Display Road Freight Order. Enter the freight order from the previous step in the Freight Order field. Click Continue, and on the next screen, the unloading instruction can be seen, as shown in Figure 4.23. Note the entry under Message Text indicating the ID for the XML message. On the next screen, check Unloading Instruction for Receiver Interface – Transportation Order Loading AppointmentRequest_IN and Processing Status Delivered, as shown in Figure 4.24. Figure 4.24 Display Unloading Instructions 9. Display the TU in SAP EWM A TU is automatically created in SAP EWM and assigned to the inbound © 249 delivery. The TU will appear under the Transportation Unit tab at the inbound delivery item level, as shown in Figure 4.25. Figure 4.25 Display TU for Inbound Delivery 10. Follow the path Inbound Processes • Receiving of Handling Unit • Rec. HU by Delivery. As shown in Figure 4.27, scan/enter an inbound delivery on the second screen and press (Enter). On the next screen, enter the product, Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 250 quantity, and batch details. Then click on Enter on the RF screen and click the F2PGR, F3CRWT, and F4CONF buttons on the final screen. Figure 4.27 Goods Receipt and Putaway 12. Input the transportation unit in the Transportation field and execute. Select More • Action • Door. Set up Departure from Door and Departure from Checkpoint, as shown in Figure 4.28. 13. sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.en: 4.3.2 Outbound Process Throughout this section, we’ll provide a comprehensive overview of the outbound goods issue process and the integration of freight orders in SAP TM. We’ll also delve into transportation planning based on sales orders in detail. Business Process As shown in Figure 4.31, the step-by-step process for outbound processes involves the following sequence: 1. A sales order is created in SAP SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 2. SAP TM receives orders and deliveries from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and utilizes the information to create transportation requirements and freight units. 3. After establishing the transportation requirements, SAP TM performs transportation planning and generates freight orders. 4. If the transportation planning is based on sales orders, SAP TM generates deliveries in the ERP system. These outbound deliveries are then forwarded to SAP EWM, which automatically generates the corresponding warehouse requests of the outbound delivery order type. 5. Based on the freight orders, SAP TM sends a loading appointment request message to SAP EWM, which creates a vehicle or TU along with planned shipping and receiving activities. © 253 6. The outbound delivery orders are assigned to TU activities. Warehouse activities, such as picking, packing, staging, and loading of goods, can be performed before the vehicle or TU arrives at the door. 7. When the vehicle or TU arrives, the Arrival at Checkpoint action is executed, and the system changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active. A door is then assigned to the vehicle or TU, and if yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door. 8. Once the warehouse activities are finished, the goods issue is posted, and transportation documents are printed. The delivery information is transferred to SAP ERP, where the deliveries are automatically updated with execution data. The information is also sent to SAP TM to update the consumed transportation requirements. 9. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard, and if not, the Departure from Door action is executed. When the Departure from Checkpoint action is executed, SAP EWM automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Active to Completed. 10. A loading appointment notification message is then transmitted to SAP TM, where the freight orders are updated with execution data. The execution status of the SAP TM freight order is set to Completed, and freight settlement is conducted in SAP TM. The freight settlement document in SAP TM serves as the foundation for invoice verification and settlement in the ERP system. sections.title: Advanced Shipping and Receiving
sections.en: 4.4 Advanced Shipping and Receiving Advanced shipping and receiving empowers individuals to efficiently send, receive, and transport goods through a comprehensive and seamless procedure. It streamlines the process from the moment a truck arrives at the gate to the ultimate receipt of goods in the warehouse by enabling mixed and multi- warehouse scenarios to be managed within a single freight order. This system allows a truck that has registered its arrival at a checkpoint to perform loading and unloading operations at a single location or to distribute goods to multiple warehouses at the same site. To create transportation requirements, both materials management and sales and distribution must be in place, and information exchange among various SAP S/4HANA application components, such as SAP TM, SAP EWM, stock room management, inventory management and physical inventory, and logistics execution is streamlined through the utilization of a unified data model. The application of the EDIFACT standard to electronic data interchange (EDI) messages and the provision of specialized applications further simplify the exchange of information. Additionally, existing apps and RF transactions for shipping and receiving processes are expanded to facilitate communication, allowing users to track the status of products throughout the shipping and receiving processes and gain valuable insights. The advanced shipping and receiving process is based on the freight order and does not utilize either the TUs or vehicles in SAP EWM.

sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.en: 4.4.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll delve into to an inbound goods receipt process using advanced shipping and receiving in SAP TM and SAP EWM. Business Process As shown in Figure 4.51, the inbound goods receipt process involves the following steps: 1. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA generates a purchase order. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 264 2. The embedded SAP TM funtionality creates a freight unit according to the freight unit building rule. 3. The freight order is created in embedded SAP TM using the previously created freight unit. 4. The inbound delivery is generated in SAP S/4HANA as a result of the delivery suggestion from the freight order in embedded SAP TM. 5. Once the inbound delivery is dispatched from SAP S/4HANA, it is created in embedded SAP EWM. The advanced shipping and receiving capability’s new freight order application is used to mark this inbound delivery as Ready for Warehouse Processing, and the corresponding warehouse operations (such as goods receipt, putaway, etc.) are carried out within this embedded SAP EWM instance. 6. Later, the inbound delivery is updated to the SAP S/4HANA delivery, and a message is sent to reflect these changes. sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.en: 4.4.2 Outbound Process The Advanced Shipping and Receiving outbound process in SAP EWM commences with sales, followed by transportation planning and warehouse processing, and concludes with the departure of the truck from the warehouse. We’ll walk through this process in detail in the following sections. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 276 Business Process As shown in Figure 4.76, the outbound delivery process with advanced shipping notifications (ASNs) involves the following steps: 1. To initiate the outbound process in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, a sales document such as a sales order or scheduling agreement is generated. This triggers the creation of freight Units for order-based planning, which are then replicated to Transportation Management. 2. In SAP TM, freight orders are created for the freight units and outbound deliveries are generated. These outbound deliveries are replicated to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA as well as to SAP EWM. 3. The pick, pack, and stage processes for the outbound delivery order are executed in the embedded EWM system. 4. Once the freight order is marked as Ready for Transportation Execution and the outbound delivery orders are marked as Ready for Shipping, the loading process can be initiated in SAP EWM via the Load or Unload Freight Orders app or an RF device. 5. Using the Load or Unload Freight Orders app in SAP Fiori, door assignment, loading, loading completion, and goods movements can be posted on the outbound delivery order. The goods movement can be posted either in SAP TM or SAP EWM. sections.title: Shipment Integration
sections.en: 4.5 Shipment Integration To transport multiple outbound delivery documents using the same means of transportation, SAP ERP utilizes shipment documents as a foundation for planning the logistics. The system converts handling units (HUs) within SAP ERP shipments into vehicles, TUs, or both, and schedules shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM. Following the completion of the warehouse operations, transport details are transmitted back to SAP ERP to facilitate freight cost settlement and invoicing.

sections.title: Transportation Planning in an ERP System
sections.en: 4.5.1 Transportation Planning in an ERP System In this section, we’ll explore the outbound transportation planning process in your ERP system followed by the execution of warehouse activities in SAP EWM. Business Process As shown in Figure 4.103, the outbound process involves the following steps: 1. In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, an outbound delivery (with reference to a sales order) is created. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA automatically distributes outbound deliveries to SAP EWM, where warehouse requests for outbound deliveries are generated. 2. To create a shipment with HUs and assign outbound deliveries, you can use SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The shipment details are then sent to SAP EWM, where a vehicle or TU and a planned shipping and receiving activity are automatically created, and the outbound delivery order is assigned to the TU activity. 3. Warehouse activities related to outbound delivery orders, such as picking, packing, staging, and loading the goods, are carried out in SAP EWM. 4. To activate the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active, you need to execute the Arrival at Checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU. Then, you can assign a door to the vehicle or TU. 5. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door. However, if yard management is not activated, the © 291 Arrival at Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed. 6. When the goods issue posting takes place in SAP EWM, the transport details are transferred to SAP ERP, where a shipment is automatically updated with the execution data. 7. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard. Conversely, if yard management is not activated, the Departure from Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed. sections.title: Transportation Planning in SAP EWM
sections.en: 4.5.2 Transportation Planning in SAP EWM In a scenario driven by SAP EWM, also referred to as SAP EWM-based transportation planning, transportation planning is performed by the SAP EWM system itself. This is achieved by creating a TU and assigning the unit to delivery. Business Process As shown in Figure 4.129, the outbound process with transportation planning in SAP EWM involves the following steps: 1. To begin, create an outbound delivery in either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and reference the sales order. 2. The system will automatically replicate the outbound delivery to SAP EWM and block its execution until planning results become available. The delivery item screen will display the DBT - Blocked (Transp. Plan) status type, indicating that SAP EWM is responsible for transportation planning. The Transportation Planning Type field in the delivery screen will have the value B - Obligatory External Planning in SAP EWM. 3. In SAP EWM, create a TU activity and assign the outbound delivery order. The system will update the delivery header’s transportation data from TU, such as the means of transport and vehicle. The outbound delivery order © 305 can now be executed, and its DBT - Blocked (Transp. Plan) status will no longer be set. 4. Create a warehouse task in SAP EWM for the outbound delivery order to move the product from a storage bin to the staging area. A warehouse order will be generated for the delivery order, and a pick-HU will be created for the warehouse task. The pick HU will be utilized as the destination HU. 5. Confirm the warehouse task in SAP EWM to move the product to the staging area for the outbound delivery order. 6. Once the TU arrives at the checkpoint in SAP EWM, the TU status will change to Activated. 7. In SAP EWM, move the TU from the checkpoint to the door. 8. Perform loading and post goods issue in SAP EWM. 9. After the goods issue has been posted, the system will replicate it from SAP EWM to SAP ERP and create an entry in the document flow of the outbound delivery in SAP ERP. 10. In SAP ERP, create and display a shipment and assign the outbound delivery. The system will send the SHPMNT05 IDoc from SAP EWM to SAP ERP, which will create an SAP ERP shipment with the assigned delivery. The new shipment will be displayed for the delivery, and the goods issue status on the header and item level will be set to Complete. The overall status of the shipment will be Planning Completed. 11. In SAP EWM, move the TU from the door back to the checkpoint. 12. Once the TU departs from the checkpoint in SAP EWM, the process is complete. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 4.6 Summary Thus concludes our chapter on transportation management. Throughout this chapter, we delved into various aspects, beginning with an overview of SAP TM. Furthermore, we explored inbound and outbound processes using freight order integration between SAP TM and SAP EWM Additionally, we examined inbound and outbound processes using the advanced shipping and receiving functionality. Finally, you learned about shipment integration and transportation planning in SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA as well as transportation planning in SAP EWM. © 319 5 Dock Appointment Scheduling Dock appointment scheduling is a proactive and anticipatory planning technique employed by companies to manage shipping docks, warehouses, and distribution centers. This method entails the allocation of designated time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks transporting inbound and outbound shipments. Moreover, the optimization of schedules for dock doors and yard operations is an integral aspect of dock scheduling. The objective of this chapter is to serve as a comprehensive manual on diverse dock management procedures and their seamless assimilation with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM). We’ll walk through the business processes for each technique, discuss the setup and primary data requirements needed to enable end-to-end testing of business scenarios, and provide a complete step-by-step process demonstration for each scenario. The integration of SAP with SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling presents a synergistic opportunity for warehouse and distribution centers to streamline and optimize their goods flow. The process entails configuring and linking the dock appointment scheduling system with SAP EWM’s inbound and outbound delivery procedures. At the outset, the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling system meticulously schedules precise time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks that ferry inbound and outbound shipments. Subsequently, this scheduling information is conveyed to SAP EWM, which then triggers the generation of inbound or outbound deliveries based on the designated time slots. Following the creation of the inbound or outbound delivery in SAP EWM, the system automatically assigns a specific dock door for the truck to utilize, based on the schedule information retrieved from SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. This approach ensures the accurate routing of trucks to designated dock doors, thereby optimizing the flow of goods. In sum, the integration of SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling with SAP EWM enables warehouse and distribution center operators Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

sections.title: Overview of Dock Appointment Scheduling
sections.en: 5.1 Overview of Dock Appointment Scheduling The process of dock scheduling is a valuable tool for businesses looking to optimize their use of resources and improve efficiency in their supply chain operations. By reducing wait times for truck drivers during the loading and unloading of goods, your business can minimize overcrowding and congestion, particularly on traditionally busy days like Mondays and Fridays. A delay in the dock scheduling process can lead to increased detention charges and negatively impact the operational margins of a warehouse. On the other hand, an accurate dock scheduling system can revolutionize warehouse dock operations and drastically improve traffic flow, leading to more efficient and cost-effective supply chain management During loading and unloading operations at docks, delays can occur, which can put pressure on warehouse operators to work quickly to meet manufacturing or distribution schedules. This rush can increase the risk of safety incidents occurring. © 321 By scheduling appointments in advance, warehouses can effectively plan and manage their staff for receiving and shipping processes, as well as allocate their equipment resources efficiently. This feature helps minimize delays and idle time for trucks waiting to be loaded or unloaded. Providing carriers with a link to your warehouse’s dock appointment system can reduce the need for phone- based or email bookings, resulting in shorter wait times and faster responses for carriers. Dock appointment scheduling systems are often integrated into warehouse or transportation management software, offering a range of helpful features. These features may include online booking portals, automated appointment confirmations, and real-time visibility into dock availability and traffic conditions. These capabilities allow for smoother, more streamlined operations, reducing wait times and improving overall efficiency in the supply chain. Efficient planning of vehicle arrivals and departures for unloading and loading goods is crucial to ensure a well-organized running of the warehouse and to balance the workload throughout the working day. Scheduling dock appointments in advance can help prevent appointment blowouts during the week and reduce the traffic on busy days at the warehouse. The ultimate goal is to ensure the efficient use of warehouse doors, parking spaces, and yard checkpoints for loading and unloading trucks from various carriers while avoiding interruptions in warehouse operations. Allowing carriers to schedule their own appointments online helps them plan their routes effectively and eliminates the need to arrive early to ensure they can pick up or deliver in a timely manner. The efficient scheduling of dock appointments can be instrumental in optimizing staffing levels and averting scenarios of understaffing or overstaffing. This optimization, in turn, can result in enhanced labor planning, a pivotal component of warehouse operations. A dock scheduling system serves as a valuable tool for capacity and resource planning, allowing for seamless communication between carriers and the system, while simultaneously providing real-time visibility to customers, warehouse personnel, suppliers, and carriers. By means of dock appointment scheduling, carriers and warehouse users can coordinate appointments for incoming vehicles or transportation units (TUs) during loading and unloading processes. The scheduling process can be executed online, meaning vendors and carriers can book appointments and track progress in real-time using software. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 322 Additionally, dock appointment scheduling software can be seamlessly integrated with warehouse management systems (WMS) or transportation management systems. Streamlined dock appointment scheduling can result in optimized hours of service, enhanced warehouse efficiency, improved partner collaboration, and augmented inventory turns. A dock scheduling system may also include reporting functionalities, such as audits on delivered loads, which can facilitate the automatic recording and transmission of compliance information. SAP provides a web browser-based application called SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. This application enables efficient planning of vehicle arrivals in warehouses and allows carriers to enroll their TUs for the yard, book time slots for loading and unloading, and view the workload at each loading point for each day. SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling can be deployed as a standalone solution or integrated with a local SAP EWM system. To use SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling functionalities, SAP has provided the standard Transaction NWBC or several SAP Fiori applications, as shown in Figure 5.1. Additionally, an SAP Fiori app called the Dock Appointment Scheduling for Carriers app is available in SAP S/4HANA to offer a user interface (UI) for carriers. When integrating SAP EWM and SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling, the scheduling appointment serves as the planning object for the transport. Planning is performed using time slots for loading points and defined capacities, with carriers collaborating via web access. In extended warehouse management (EWM), the TU is the processing object for the transport. Figure 5.1 SAP Fiori Apps for SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling The integration of SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling with a local SAP EWM system allows for the linkage of loading appointments with TU or vehicle © 323 activities in SAP EWM. This integration facilitates the exchange of loading appointment status updates and related TU activity information between SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling and SAP EWM. Additionally, the shipping cockpit in SAP EWM can be used to track outbound loading appointments created in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Overall, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling provides several benefits for both inbound and outbound processes. The requirements for integrating SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following: 1. You have enabled the business function SCM_EWM_FND (EWM, Essential Foundation Functions). 2. You have configured the Basis customization setting for SAP EWM. 3. Within SAP EWM, you have established configurations for means of transport. Additionally, you have created a connection between packaging materials and TUs via the SAP Easy Access menu transaction. 4. Within SAP EWM, you have defined a number range for the TU. Note that the number range for TU numbers must not be the same as the number range for the loading appointment numbers. 5. You have defined a number range for vehicles in SAP EWM, if applicable. 6. You have defined a number range for shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM. 7. You have defined a number range for appointment numbers under the customization path in SAP EWM. Some crucial concepts utilized in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following: Docking locations A docking location refers to a collection of loading points, such as a warehouse or distribution center, and represents the physical location of these loading points. This element allows for the definition of attributes that are uniform across the entire location, such as an address. If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling in conjunction with SAP EWM, a docking location represents an SAP EWM warehouse in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. You can specify if the loading points are integrated with SAP EWM within the docking location. Imperative is that the integration Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 324 with SAP EWM be consistent for all the loading points in a docking location, as well as the docking location itself. Docking locations can be established by a user with role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR. Loading points Loading appointments for vehicles are organized based on loading points. A loading point represents a group of warehouse docks that share the same processing characteristics, such as loading or unloading. In practice, these “docks” could be fuel dispensers, loading docks, or any location where goods are received or dispatched from a warehouse. You can combine the loading points of a particular geographical location into a docking location. When using docking locations, a crucial requirement is that the integration with SAP EWM is consistent for all the loading points belonging to a docking location as well as for the docking location itself. However, if docking locations are not used, you can specify whether a loading point is integrated with SAP EWM for each loading point individually. Loading appointments are scheduled at the loading point level, which is a collection of warehouse docks with similar attributes. Each loading point is allocated a defined time slot duration and a range of appointment numbers. Loading points can be established by a user with the role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR. Time slots To plan the times for loading appointments, time slots are used. The duration of each time slot is defined within the loading point and is fixed across all time slots. When creating loading points and assigning them to a docking location, the time slot duration can be specified in the docking location. The system will automatically use this duration for new loading points. When modifying a time slot duration is necessary, such as when using a greater number of time slots with shorter durations to enhance planning, you can change this duration individually in each loading point. This modification has no impact on previously generated time slots and their loading appointments and only applies to new time slots generated for upcoming time frames. A user with the role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR can create time slots. Time slot management This function allows you to create time slots for a loading point and adjust its capacity. The fixed duration of each time slot is defined in the loading point’s © 325 master data. Each time slot has a capacity, which indicates the maximum number of vehicles that can be loaded or unloaded simultaneously during that time slot. To create time slots, you would define the working time of the loading point by specifying the start date of the first time slot and specify the capacity for each time slot according to the circumstances at that time. In this way, you can adjust the capacity for each time slot by taking into account factors such as staff availability. If you’re using the graphical view, you can set the capacity for time slots for one day and then copy these values forward to the next day. Once you’ve created the time slot capacity for the week, you can carry these values forward for the next several weeks. The system automatically sets the capacity to 0 for days when the loading point is not available, such as public holidays, based on the factory calendar assigned to the loading point. You can also change the capacity of time slots for a loading point or delete all future time slots for a loading appointment after a certain date. If you need to delete time slots in the future that already have loading appointments associated with them, you must cancel the loading appointments. If you want to delete a loading point, you must delete all the time slots and appointments associated with it. Appointment management This function enables you to create and edit loading appointments for loading points. You can use loading appointments to plan vehicle arrivals at your warehouse and to balance the workload across the working day. You can assign more than one time slot to a loading appointment. In this way, you can plan flexibly for loading appointments that require different amounts of time for loading or unloading. For example, in a loading point with a time slot duration of 15 minutes, you can create one loading appointment that lasts for 30 minutes, perhaps to unload a small delivery, and then create another loading appointment that lasts for 90 minutes, perhaps to unload a larger delivery with more handling units (HUs). Appointments of variable duration You can create loading appointments of different durations by assigning more than one time slot to a loading appointment. The shortest loading appointment possible is one time slot. The longest loading appointment possible is 7 days. Each loading appointment must Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 326 consist of consecutive time slots. If you need to create a loading appointment that includes some time when no workers are available at the loading point, you must include this time in the duration of the appointment. Provisional appointments When working with docking locations, you can create loading appointments for a docking location without specifying a loading appointment, without specifying time slots, or both. These loading appointments have the status Provisional. Provisional appointments do not fill any capacity in a loading point, and you cannot process provisional appointments without further planning. When you enter a loading point and time slots into a provisional appointment, the loading appointment status changes to Planned, and it fills capacity at the loading point. You can then proceed with the loading appointment. Managing loading appointments You can change loading appointments, when the expected vehicle has not yet arrived at its checkpoint, to different time slots in the loading point. However, appointment planners for carriers can change the time slots of their loading appointments only if the restricted planning period has not begun. As long as both loading points are in the same docking location, you can change a loading appointment to a different loading point if the vehicle has not yet arrived at the warehouse. If you’re using docking locations, the new loading point must have the same docking location as the original loading point. You can cancel loading appointments if the vehicle has not yet arrived at the checkpoint. Indicating loading appointment direction You can specify whether a loading appointment is an inbound appointment or an outbound appointment, if required. Creating loading appointments for time slots without free capacity You can create loading appointments for a time slot at your loading point even if there is no free capacity for the slot. However, appointment planners for carriers can create loading appointments for time slots with free capacity only. Indicating that a loading appointment has arrived at the dock If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling without integration with SAP EWM, you can indicate that a vehicle has arrived at the dock without © 327 first indicating that the vehicle has arrived at the checkpoint. You can also indicate that a vehicle has departed from the checkpoint without first indicating that the vehicle has departed from the dock. Changing the date and time after the action is performed SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling saves a record of the time when you update the status of each loading appointment. You can change the date and time related to actions for the loading appointment after the actions are performed. For example, if you set the status of a loading appointment to Departed from Checkpoint later than when the vehicle actually left, you can enter the actual time of departure in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. You can then store these actual times for later analysis. Appointments can be created by a user with the role DAS_EXT_CARR_PLANNER. Table 5.1 provides further information on the various roles involved in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Role Role Description /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR Administrator for Dock Appointment Scheduling /SCWM/DAS_SPECIALIST Specialist for Dock Appointment Scheduling /SCWM/DAS_CP_CLERK Checkpoint Clerk for Dock Appointment Scheduling /SCWM/DAS_EXT_CARR_PLANNER Appointment Planner for Carrier in Dock Appointment Scheduling /SCWM/EWM_TO_DAS_INTEGRATION Technical Role for EWM Integration to Dock Appointment Scheduling Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 328 Role Role Description /SCWM/DAS_TO_EWM_INTEGRATION Technical Role for Dock Appointment Scheduling Integration to EWM Table 5.1 Role Matrix Your options for SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following: Appointment TU (planning in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling) As shown in Figure 5.2, in this option, an appointment is generated in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling, which triggers the automatic creation of a TU in SAP EWM. Figure 5.2 Appointment Creates TU TU creates appointment (planning in SAP EWM) As shown in Figure 5.3, TU is generated in SAP EWM, which triggers loading appointments in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.
