sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.en: 7.2.2 Outbound Process An outbound scenario with SAP Yard Logistics typically involves managing the movement of goods or materials from a warehouse or distribution center to the outbound transportation area, such as a trucking terminal or a loading dock. Yard logistics play a crucial role in ensuring efficient and streamlined operations during the outbound process. We’ll look at the outbound process in detail in the following sections. Business Process As shown in Figure 7.33, the outbound goods issue process using SAP Yard Logistics involves the following steps: 1. The first step in this process is to create a sales order for a customer in the ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. The sales order is then converted into an outbound delivery, which is automatically sent to SAP EWM for warehouse processing. 2. Once the planning is complete, the shipment is distributed to both SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics to initiate the process of truck arrival, loading, and departure. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 442 3. The ERP message triggers the creation of the Yard Request document, which is used to plan the first yard activity. This message is also sent to SAP EWM, where a TU document is created containing information about the planned content. Additionally, automatic door determination or manual door assignment takes place, allowing SAP EWM to start the picking and staging process. 4. It’s important to note that since SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM are involved in this process, yard activities such as check-in posting or movements should not be executed. These steps fall under the scope of SAP Yard Logistics. 5. While the warehouse begins its activities in the yard, the Yard Order is created based on the Yard Request. This document is used for processing in the yard, and since this is an outbound scenario, an outbound Yard Order is created. For the arrival of the truck, an inbound yard order is required, which can be generated from the outbound Yard Order. 6. Meanwhile, in SAP EWM, outbound processes are occurring, and the products are being staged. Simultaneously, various yard activities are taking place in SAP Yard Logistics. Once the movement to the door is activated, another door determination may occur, either when no door determination has been triggered before or to validate the previously determined door. 7. With the confirmation of the TU in SAP Yard Logistics, the arrival at the door is posted in SAP EWM. At this point, the TU cannot be moved in the yard any longer, and yard activities are only possible again after receiving notification from SAP EWM that loading is complete. 8. This notification triggers yard activities, and the movement from the door to the next yard location, such as the checkpoint for departure, can be executed. A departure from door message is sent from SAP Yard Logistics to SAP EWM. 9. Goods issue may be triggered in SAP EWM during this process, and the latest possible point for the goods issue posting is the checkout of the TU. After the loading notification is sent to SAP Yard Logistics, no further yard activities are allowed in SAP EWM, and all postings occur in the yard. 10. Now that the truck has reached the outbound checkpoint, the check-out can be posted, which is also sent to SAP EWM and triggers the check-out © 443 posting there. The ERP documents will be updated from SAP EWM based on the goods issue and check-out posting. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 7.3 Summary That’s it! You’re now prepared work on integrating SAP Yard Logistics with SAP EWM. In this chapter, we provided an overview of SAP Yard Logistics, focusing on the benefits of implementing SAP Yard Logistics. We also compared SAP Yard Logistics with yard management and explored the integration of SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics. Furthermore, we covered an inbound goods receipt process and an outbound goods issue process leveraging the integration of SAP EWM, SAP Yard Logistics, and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 460 8 Environmental Health and Safety The SAP Environment, Health, and Safety Management (SAP EHS Management) module represents an all-encompassing system meticulously crafted to effectively govern and oversee environmental health and safety (EHS) risks within an organization. This module empowers enterprises to diligently trace and ascertain compliance with regulatory requisites, proactively identify and mitigate workplace hazards, and instill a culture ingrained with safety consciousness among employees. Encompassing myriad aspects such as incident management, risk assessment, safety training, emergency response planning, and compliance reporting, the SAP EHS Management module emerges as a robust framework to uphold the highest standards of health and safety. The primary objective of this chapter is to explicate the intricacies of the SAP EHS Management repertoire —and its seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through the embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM) framework. This SAP component offers comprehensive support for all activities pertaining to product safety and stewardship. If your organization manufactures and sells substances that are potentially harmful, it is of utmost importance to safeguard human beings and the environment from the risks associated with these substances. Additionally, you must comply with numerous laws and regulations concerning hazardous substances on a global scale. This SAP component aids in the secure handling of hazardous substances, ensuring their safe introduction to the market and automating compliance with all relevant regulations. SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM are distinct modules within an SAP system. The integration of these two modules facilitates a more efficient and streamlined management of hazardous materials and related processes. The opening section of this chapter provides an overview of EHS concerns and emphasizes the key functionalities of SAP EHS Management. We subsequently focus on the various options available for an inbound process using SAP EHS Management, encompassing business processes, configuration, master data, and a comprehensive demonstration of the end-to-end process. sections.title: Overview of Environmental Health Safety
sections.en: 8.1 Overview of Environmental Health Safety EHS is a broad term to describe the laws, rules, regulations, professions, programs, and workplace efforts that aim to protect the health and safety of employees and the public, as well as the environment, from hazards associated with the workplace. Essentially, EHS encompasses the profession of occupational safety and health professionals, along with their colleagues in the environmental department. EHS is a discipline that focuses on protecting the health and safety of people, as well as preserving the natural environment. The primary objective of EHS is to prevent accidents, injuries, and illnesses in the workplace, while minimizing the impact of business operations on the environment. The roles and functions of EHS professionals may vary depending on the organization and industry, but typically include the following: Developing and implementing safety policies and procedures: EHS professionals are responsible for developing and enforcing safety policies and procedures to ensure compliance with regulations and standards. Conducting safety training and education: EHS professionals provide safety training to employees to ensure they have the knowledge and skills to work safely and prevent accidents. Conducting safety inspections and audits: EHS professionals conduct safety inspections and audits to identify hazards and risks and recommend corrective actions. Investigating accidents and incidents: EHS professionals investigate accidents and incidents to determine their root causes and to recommend corrective actions and prevent similar incidents in the future. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 462 Managing hazardous materials and waste: EHS professionals manage hazardous materials and waste to ensure they are handled, stored, and disposed of safely and in compliance with regulations. Developing and implementing environmental programs: EHS professionals develop and implement programs to manage environmental risks, such as air and water pollution, waste management, and energy conservation. Overall, the role of EHS professionals is to ensure the safety and well-being of employees, protect the environment, and maintain regulatory compliance in the workplace. In another words, EHS is a discipline that focuses on implementing practical measures to protect the environment and ensure health and safety in the workplace. From a safety standpoint, it involves creating organized procedures to identify workplace hazards and reduce accidents and exposure to harmful situations and substances. Additionally, personnel are trained in accident prevention, emergency preparedness, and the use of protective clothing and equipment. At its core, EHS aims to develop safe, high-quality, and environmentally friendly processes, working practices, and systemic activities that prevent or reduce the risk of harm to people in general, to operators, or to patients. From an environmental standpoint, EHS involves implementing a systematic approach to comply with regulations regarding waste management, air emissions, and reducing a site’s carbon footprint. Regulatory requirements are essential in the EHS discipline, and EHS managers must identify and understand relevant regulations, communicating their implications to executive management so that the company can implement appropriate measures. In the United States, organizations are subject to EHS regulations outlined in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), particularly CFR 29, 40, and 49. However, EHS management is not limited to legal compliance, and companies are encouraged to go beyond what is required by law as appropriate. SAP EHS Management is a software solution provided by SAP designed to help organizations manage their EHS risks and compliance requirements. This integrated solution allows organizations to manage their EHS data, processes, and reporting in a single system. SAP EHS Management works by providing a range of modules that allow organizations to manage their EHS data and processes. These modules include: © 463 Product safety This module allows organizations to manage the safety of their products by tracking and reporting on hazardous substances, chemical compliance, and labeling requirements. Dangerous goods management This module allows organizations to manage the transportation and storage of hazardous materials in compliance with local and international regulations. Waste management This module allows organizations to manage their waste management processes, including waste generation, storage, and disposal. Occupational health This module allows organizations to manage the health and safety of their employees, including monitoring and reporting on workplace hazards and incidents. Industrial hygiene and safety This module allows organizations to manage their industrial hygiene and safety processes, including risk assessments, inspections, and audits. Environ ment This module allows organizations to manage their environmental compliance requirements, including air and water quality monitoring, emissions reporting, and sustainability reporting. SAP EHS Management provides various features that assist organizations in maintaining employee health and safety, product and reach compliance, product safety, and environmental compliance management, including the following: Employee health and safety This functionality deals with processes related to industrial hygiene and occupational health to ensure the well-being of workers and the workplace. When workers handle dangerous substances, they must follow specific guidelines, and SAP EHS Management simplifies this process. Additionally, it incorporates risk management and asset management processes and places risk data into work orders, along with proposing safety measures. Product and reach compliance This functionality helps organizations maintain records of materials and Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 464 products while upholding compliance regulations for their industries. It establishes compliance workflows, and authorities can assign guidelines and legal necessities to business operations, ensuring the safety of production materials and final products. Product safety This functionality helps organizations meet their legal, safety, and sustainability responsibilities while maintaining the supply chain of products. It also maintains regulations for product storage, packaging, and transportation. Environmental compliance management This functionality maintains different environmental laws and regulations, allowing organizations to track air and water emissions records to ensure environmental safety. All environment-related activities and tasks can be tracked using this feature of SAP EHS Management. SAP EHS Management provides numerous benefits, including the following capabilities: Maintaining industrial hygiene and occupational health programs Analyzing operational data to anticipate hazards and taking steps to reduce them Sharing data, integrating business processes, and sharing workflows to strengthen the EHS process Safeguarding operational continuity by identifying and moderating safety risks Assisting organizations in following legal and safety guidelines, thus preventing accidental expenses Enhancing the safety norms of business operations Analyzing accidents efficiently to avoid them in the future Incorporating risk management strategies into daily business activities, thus reducing the chances of risk and creating awareness among workers Creating and implementing health surveillance agreements Preparing surveys and tasks to collect information about working environment conditions © 465 SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM are two different modules within an SAP system. The integration of these two modules allows for a more efficient and streamlined management of hazardous materials and other related processes. The integration of SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM involves several key steps, including: 1. Configuring the necessary settings in both SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM: This step involves setting up the relevant organizational structures, material master data, and other necessary master data in both modules. 2. Defining EHS-related classes for hazardous materials in SAP EWM: These classes are used to identify and manage hazardous materials in the warehouse and transportation processes. 3. Replicating master data between SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM: This step involves setting up the interfaces and data transfer mechanisms between the two modules, allowing for the exchange of data such as material safety data sheets (MSDS), product safety data sheets (PSDS), and other relevant data. 4. Setting up safety stock and inventory management in SAP EWM: This step ensures that the required safety stock levels are maintained for hazardous materials and that inventory levels are accurately tracked and managed. 5. Executing EHS-related functions within SAP EWM: This step includes handling hazardous materials, waste disposal, and other related processes within a warehouse. Overall, the integration of SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM provides a comprehensive solution for managing hazardous materials, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and reducing the risk of accidents and incidents in the warehouse and transportation processes Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 466

sections.title: Goods Receipt and Goods Issue Process Using
sections.en: 8.2 Goods Receipt and Goods Issue Process Using SAP EHS Management In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the goods receipt and goods issue process using SAP EHS Management. We’ll begin with the inbound process. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process, configuration, and master data setup needed and then provide a process demonstration.

sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.en: 8.2.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the inbound goods receipt process using SAP EHS Management by utilizing embedded EWM. This section is divided into four parts: inbound goods receipt business process, configuration needed for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow. Business Process As shown in Figure 8.1, an inbound process in SAP EWM involves the receiving and storage of goods in a warehouse or distribution center. The business process for the receipt and putaway of hazardous material is involves the following steps: 1. A purchase order for hazardous materials is generated in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The purchase order triggers the automatic creation of an inbound delivery, which is then replicated to SAP EWM in the background. 2. When the material is physically received in the warehouse, the warehouse team generates a warehouse task and physically places the material in the hazardous storage area in the SAP EWM system. A putaway strategy is defined for hazardous materials, guiding warehouse operators to physically store the material in the designated hazardous area and confirm the warehouse task accordingly. 3. After the material is stored in the hazardous area, the warehouse team performs a goods receipt in SAP EWM, which generates inventory in both the SAP EWM and SAP S/4HANA systems. © 467 Figure 8.1 Inbound Process Using SAP EHS Management Configuration In this section, we’ll cover the key customization steps required for this process, assuming that the main SAP EWM customization settings have already been configured in the system: 1. Define a storage type for storing hazardous material This configuration setting is needed to store hazardous material in designated storage area. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Define Storage Types. To define a storage type for hazardous material, on the Change View “Define Storage Types”: Details screen, click New Entries. For the Hazard.Sub.Mgmt field, make sure the value selected is 2 - Haz.sub.check at stor.type and stor.section levels or verify these settings meet your business requirements, as shown in Figure 8.2. Figure 8.2 Define Storage Type Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 468 2. Define storage sections for the hazardous material storage type In this configuration setting, storage sections will be defined. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Define Storage Section. Click New Entries in the Change View “Define Storage Sections”: Overview screen and create the storage section, as shown in Figure 8.3. Figure 8.3 Define Storage Section 3. Assign permitted hazard rating 1 to each storage type In this IMG activity, you assign the allowed hazard rating 1 for each storage type. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Hazardous Substance • Assign Permitted Hazard Rating 1 for Each Storage Type. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse Number and Storage Type fields and enter “1” in the HazrR (hazard rating) field, as shown in Figure 8.4. Figure 8.4 Assign Permitted Hazard Rating 1 for Each Storage Type 4. Assign permitted hazard rating 2 to each storage type In this IMG activity, you assign the allowed hazard rating 2 for each storage type. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Hazardous Substance • Assign Permitted Hazard Rating 2 for Each Storage Type. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse Number and Storage Type fields and enter “2” in the HazrR (hazard rating) field, as shown in Figure 8.5. © 469 Figure 8.5 Assign Permitted Hazard Rating 2 for Each Storage Type 5. Define the storage type search sequence for putaway In this IMG activity, you assign the storage type search sequence for putaway. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage Type Search • Define Storage Type Search for Putaway. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse No. and Stor.Type Srch Seq (storage type search sequence) fields, as shown in Figure 8.6. Figure 8.6 Storage Type Search for Putaway 6. Assign a storage type to the storage type search sequence This configuration setting is needed to assign storage type. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage Type Search • Assign Storage type to Storage Type Search Sequence. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse No., Storage Type, and Stor.Type Srch Seq (storage type search sequence) fields, as shown in Figure 8.7. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 470 Figure 8.7 Assign Storage Type to Storage Type Search Sequence 7. Define the putaway control indicator for putaway process This configuration setting is needed for the putaway control indicator. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage type Search • Define Putaway Control Indicator. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse No, Putaway Control, and Stor.Type Srch Seq fields, as shown in Figure 8.8. Figure 8.8 Define Putaway Control Indicator for Putaway Process 8. Specify the storage type search sequence for putaway process This configuration setting is needed to assign hazardous ratings to the search sequence. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage type Search • Specify Storage Type Search Sequence. Click New Entries and maintain the WhN (warehouse number), Proc/… (process type), HazRat1 (hazard rating 1), HazRat2 (hazard rating 2), and Srch Seq. (search sequence) fields, as shown in Figure 8.9. © 471 Figure 8.9 Specify Storage Type Search Sequence for Putaway Process 9. Create storage section search indicators for putaway process This configuration setting is needed to assign storage sections. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage Section Search • Create Storage Section Indicators. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse and SecIn (storage section) fields, as shown in Figure 8.10. Figure 8.10 Storage Section Indicators for Putaway Process 10. Maintain the storage section search sequence for putaway process This configuration setting is needed to maintain the storage search sequence. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies • Storage Section Search • Maintain Storage Section Search Sequence. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse No., Storage Type, Haz. Rating 1, Haz. Rating 2, Stor.Sect.Ind (storage section indicator), and Storage Section fields, as shown in Figure 8.11. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 472 Figure 8.11 Maintain Storage Section Search Sequence for Putaway Process 11. Assign storage bin types to storage types This configuration setting assigns storage bin types to storage types. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Receipt Process • Strategies Storage Bin Determination • Assign Storage Bin Types to Storage Types. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse Number, Storage Type, and Storage Bin Type fields, as shown in Figure 8.12. Figure 8.12 Assign Storage Bin Types to Storage Types Master Data Setup In this section, we’ll go through the important master data setup needed for this process: 1. Create a material in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA In this master data setup, you can create a hazardous material via the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • Materials Management • Material Master • Material • Create (General) • Immediately or via Transaction MM01. The material master used for our business process scenario is EWMS4-HAZMAT. To assign a relevant hazardous rating in Material Master in SAP S/4HANA, click the WM Execution tab and select the Relevant for HS checkbox, as shown in Figure 8.13. © 473 Figure 8.13 Create Material Master 2. Display warehouse product in SAP EWM To display a warehouse product in SAP EWM, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product • Maintain Warehouse Product or execute Transaction /SCWM/MAT1, click the Storage tab and select the Haz.Sub.Strg.Rel for the product master, as shown in Figure 8.14. Figure 8.14 Display Warehouse Product 3. Maintain warehouse products in SAP EWM You can maintain warehouse data for the product master by following the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product • Maintain Warehouse Product or executing Transaction /SCWM/MAT1. Click the Warehouse tab and maintain the Putaway Control, Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 474 Storage Section Ind., and Storage Bin Type fields for the product master, as shown in Figure 8.15. 4. Maintain products in SAP EWM storage type capacity control You can maintain storage type capacities for the product master by following the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product • Maintain Warehouse Product or executing Transaction /SCWM/MAT1. Click the St. Type Data tab and maintain the Storage Type and Maximum Quantity fields, as shown in Figure 8.16. Figure 8.15 Maintain Warehouse Product Figure 8.16 Storage Type Capacity Control 5. Create hazardous substance master : basic data To maintain hazardous substance master data, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • SCM Basis • PS&S Services • Hazardous Substance Management • Hazardous Substance Master • HSMD - Edit Hazardous Substance Master or execute Transaction HSMD. Click the Basic Data tab and maintain the Haz. Rating 1 and Haz Rating 2 fields, as shown in Figure 8.17. © 475 6. Create hazardous substance master: additional data To maintain product safety and stewardship master data, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • SCM Basis • PS&S Services • Hazardous Substance Management • Hazardous Substance Master • HSMD - Edit Hazardous Substance Master or execute Transaction HSMD. To create text types for the material master in SAP S/4HANA, click the Additional Data tab and maintain the text types via the TxtTy. column, as shown in Figure 8.18. Figure 8.17 Create Hazardous Substance Master Figure 8.18 Create Hazardous Substance Master Note This represents a tailored solution in accordance with specific business requirements. Process Demo In this section, we’ll go through an inbound process using SAP EHS Management step by step: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 476 1. Create a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create a purchase order, execute Transaction ME21N. Input the supplier, material, purchase order quantity, plant, and receiving storage location and other mandatory required details. For example, the value in the Conf. Control field should be 0004 Inbound Delivery. Press (Enter) to create the purchase order, as shown in Figure 8.19. Figure 8.19 Create a Purchase Order 2. Create an inbound delivery with reference to the purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To create an inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL31N, enter supplier and purchase order detail and other details according to your business requirements on the initial screen and click Continue, as shown in Figure 8.20. Note the inbound delivery number, which you’ll need for the next step. 3. Display an inbound delivery in SAP EWM To display the inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL33N. Enter the delivery number from the previous step and click Continue, as shown in Figure 8.21. 4. Create a putaway warehouse task in SAP EWM To perform putaway, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Input the inbound delivery in the Find field after selecting Logistics Execution Delivery and click Execute. Select the line item for the delivery and, via the menu bar, select Inbound Delivery • Follow on functions • Warehouse task to create the putaway warehouse task. Finally, click Create + Save on the screen, as shown in Figure 8.22. © 477 Figure 8.20 Create Inbound Delivery Figure 8.21 Display an Inbound Delivery Figure 8.22 Create Putaway Warehouse Task 5. Display logs of hazardous ratings in SAP EWM You can view the putaway warehouse task indicating product hazardous ratings and perform the putaway in Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Input the inbound delivery and click Execute. Select the line item and, in the header, via the menu bar, select Inbound Delivery • Follow On functions • Warehouse task to create a putaway warehouse task. Then, review the log by clicking the Log button in the standard toolbar. Select the Product WT Creation log, as shown in Figure 8.23. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 478 Figure 8.23 Display Logs of Hazardous Ratings 6. Display logs of capacity checks in SAP EWM A capacity check is performed during putaway. To perform putaway, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Input the inbound delivery and click Execute. Select the line item and, in the header, select Follow on Functions • Warehouse task to create a putaway warehouse task. Then, review the log by clicking the Log button in the standard toolbar. Select Capacity check against storage bin, as shown in Figure 8.24. Figure 8.24 Display Logs of Capacity Check 7. Confirm putaway task To confirm the putaway warehouse task, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Select Inbound Documents • Inbound Delivery • Warehouse Order and enter a warehouse order in the field Warehouse Order and click Execute. Select a warehouse order line item, select More • Methods • Confirm warehouse task in the background. Once confirmed, the status of the warehouse order should be C - Confirmed, as shown in Figure 8.25. Figure 8.25 Confirm Putaway Task © 479 8. Display hazardous material stock in SAP EWM To display the stock of hazardous materials, execute Transaction /SCWM/ILHS, input the Warehouse No. and click Execute. The hazardous material stock will be displayed, as shown in Figure 8.26. Figure 8.26 Display Hazardous Material Stock in SAP EWM Note The inbound goods receipt process using SAP EWM, SAP EHS Management, and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is now complete.

sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.en: 8.2.2 Outbound Process In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the outbound goods issue process using SAP EHS Management by utilizing embedded EWM. This section is divided into four parts: business process, configuration needed for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow. Business Process As shown in Figure 8.27, an outbound process with SAP EWM and SAP EHS Management involves the following steps: 1. The outbound process typically starts in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when a sales order is created. An outbound delivery is created in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA with reference to the sales order, This outbound delivery is automatically is replicated in SAP EWM for further processing. 2. In SAP EWM, a wave is created for the outbound delivery order. Upon wave release, a warehouse task to pick the hazardous material is automatically created and is based on the picking strategy for the hazardous material. 3. Hazardous material is further picked, packed, and loaded as per the warehouse process. Once the process is complete, the warehouse team Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 480 performs the goods issue for the outbound delivery order, and the outbound process is completed. Figure 8.27 Outbound Process Using SAP EHS Management Configuration In this section, we’ll go through the important configuration steps needed for outbound processes using SAP EHS Management: 1. Define storage type search sequence This configuration setting is needed to specify the storage type search sequence. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process • Strategies • Specify Storage Type Search Sequence. Click New Entries and maintain warehouse and storage type to specify the stock removal indicator, as shown in Figure 8.28. Figure 8.28 Define Storage Type Search Sequence 2. Determine the storage type search sequence for stock removal This configuration setting determines the storage type search sequence for stock removal. Follow the IMG menu path SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Goods Issue Process • Strategies • Determine Storage Type Search Sequence for Stock Removal. Click New Entries and maintain the Warehouse, Stock Removal © 481 Indicator, Warehouse Process Type, HazRat1 (hazardous rating 1), HazRat2 (hazardous rating 2), Storage Type, and RemR (stock removal rule) fields, as shown in Figure 8.29. Figure 8.29 Determine Storage Type Search Sequence for Stock Removal Master Data Setup Only one master data step is required for this process: maintaining the pick control indicator in SAP EWM. To maintain this indicator for the product master, follow the SAP Easy Access menu path Logistics • SCM Extended Warehouse Management • Extended Warehouse Management • Master Data • Product • Maintain Warehouse Product or execute Transaction /SCWM/MAT1. Click the Warehouse tab and maintain the Storage Removal Indicator field, as shown in Figure 8.30. Figure 8.30 Display Warehouse Product Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 482 Process Demo In this section, we’ll go through the outbound process using SAP EHS Management step by step: 1. Initiate a customer sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA To a create sales order, execute Transaction VA01. Enter Order type and Sales area details. Click Continue and, on the next screen, enter all the required details for sales order creation, such as material, quantity, and plant, as shown in Figure 8.31, and save. Note the sales order number, which you’ll need for the next step. 2. Create an outbound delivery with reference to a sales order To create an outbound delivery, execute Transaction VL01N. Input the sales order from the previous step and enter a shipping point on the initial screen. Next, press (Enter) to create the outbound delivery, as shown in Figure 8.32. Note the outbound delivery number, which you’ll need for the next step. Figure 8.31 Create Sales Order Figure 8.32 Create Outbound Delivery © 483 3. Display the outbound delivery order in SAP EWM To display the outbound delivery in SAP EWM, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDO. Input the delivery number from the previous step in the Logistics Execution Delivery field and press (Enter). The outbound delivery order will be displayed, as shown in Figure 8.33. Figure 8.33 Display Outbound Delivery Order 4. Create the pick warehouse task for picking hazardous material in SAP EWM To create the pick warehouse task, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDO. Input Logistics Execution Delivery from the previous step and select Outbound Delivery order • Follow on Function • Create Warehouse Task. Select the line item and click Create + Save to create the warehouse task, as shown in Figure 8.34. Figure 8.34 Create Pick Warehouse Task for Picking Hazardous Material 5. Confirm the pick warehouse task for hazardous material in SAP EWM To the confirm pick warehouse task, execute Transaction /SCWM/MON. Select Outbound • Documents • Outbound Delivery Order • Warehouse order and input the warehouse order from the previous step in the Warehouse Order field. Confirm the warehouse order/task on this screen. Once confirmed, its status should be C - Confirmed, as shown in Figure 8.35. 6. Perform the goods issue for the outbound delivery order To perform the goods issue for outbound delivery order, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDO. In the Find field, select Outbound Delivery Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 484 Order, and enter the delivery number from and click Goods Issue. The goods issue status should be Confirmed, as shown in Figure 8.36. Figure 8.35 Confirm Pick Warehouse Task for Hazardous Material Figure 8.36 Perform Goods Issue Note The outbound goods issue process using SAP EWM, SAP EHS Management, and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is now complete. © 485

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 8.3 Summary That’s it! You’re now prepared to work on EHS processes in your own company. In this chapter, we provided an overview of EHS in general and explored the benefits of SAP EHS Management specifically. Additionally, we delved into the available deployment options for integrating SAP EHS Management with SAP EWM and SAP ERP. Furthermore, we covered inbound and outbound processes using the integration of SAP EWM, SAP EHS Management, and either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 486 9 Plant Maintenance Plant maintenance is a sophisticated module incorporated within the SAP’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, specifically designed to assist organizations in effectively managing and up keeping their plants, equipment, and assets. Its purpose is to optimize maintenance procedures, minimize downtime, and enhance overall operational efficiency. By utilizing plant maintenance, your company can bolster asset reliability, reduce maintenance costs, and elevate its overall operational effectiveness. The primary objective of this chapter is to furnish you with a comprehensive understanding of plant maintenance. Plant maintenance is an integral part of SAP ERP helps enterprises manage and preserve their equipment and systems. The plant maintenance application component is a comprehensive tool to streamline maintenance activities. With plant maintenance, an organization can automate repairs and optimize maintenance requests. This application allows users to document issues within the SAP system, plan labor and material activities, and track and settle costs. The integration of SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) with plant maintenance is crucial for optimizing the handling of goods in the maintenance process. By integrating these two systems, an organization can ensure efficient coordination between warehouse operations and maintenance activities. This chapter begins with an overview of plant maintenance, highlighting its key benefits and the advantages of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM. We also cover various scenarios and functionalities related to plant maintenance- SAP EWM integration, specifically focusing on outbound processes and return (inbound) processes using plant maintenance orders. This chapter provides detailed information about the business processes, configuration, and master data and offers an end-to-end demonstration of the entire process. Emphasis will be placed on plant maintenance, which is an SAP system meticulously tailored to cater to the requirements of maintaining your plants. The central focus of this chapter is on providing an overview of plant maintenance and elucidating the various involved processes. We will offer meticulous insights into the plant maintenance process, coupled with a step-by- ©

sections.title: Overview of Plant Maintenance
sections.en: 9.1 Overview of Plant Maintenance Plant maintenance encompasses a range of activities to help an organization manage its technical systems effectively. These activities include inspection, preventive maintenance, and repair, among other measures. Inspection involves conducting a thorough assessment of the current condition of a technical system. This task involves checking the equipment and components of the system to identify any potential issues or areas of concern. The data collected from inspections can be used to create maintenance plans to address the specific needs of the system. Preventive maintenance aims to keep technical systems in an ideal condition by regularly carrying out routine maintenance activities. This area includes tasks like cleaning, lubricating, adjusting, and replacing components before they fail. By implementing preventive maintenance, your organization can reduce the risk of breakdowns and extend equipment lifespans. Repair involves fixing any issues that arise within the technical system to restore it to its ideal condition. This activity can involve replacing defective components, repairing broken equipment, or adjusting components that are not working properly. Repair work is usually carried out in response to an identified problem or issue. Other measures taken using the plant maintenance capabilities can include planning and scheduling maintenance tasks, monitoring equipment performance, and managing spare parts inventory. These activities support the overall goal of keeping technical systems functioning efficiently and effectively. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 488 In general, the plant maintenance business process involves the following end- to-end functions: Request initiation A maintenance request is generated indicating the need for maintenance or repair work to be performed at an external location. This request can come from various sources such as equipment operators, technicians, or automated monitoring systems. Work order creation Based on the maintenance request, a work order is created, specifying the details of the task, including the equipment or system to be repaired, the location, the required resources, and any relevant documentation or procedures. Resource allocation The necessary resources for the maintenance task are identified and allocated. These resources might include skilled technicians, specialized tools or equipment, spare parts, and transportation arrangements to reach the external location. Planning and scheduling The maintenance task is planned and scheduled, considering factors such as technician availability, priority of the task, and the logistics of reaching the external site. The schedule should optimize efficiency and minimize downtime. Dispatching and logistics Once the schedule is finalized, the work order is dispatched to the assigned technicians or maintenance crew. Logistics arrangements, such as arranging transportation or providing detailed directions to the external site, are made to ensure timely arrival. Execution Technicians travel to the external site and carry out the maintenance or repair work according to the specifications outlined in the work order. They may perform inspections, diagnostics, troubleshooting, repairs, replacements, or any other necessary tasks to restore the equipment or system to proper working condition. Documentation and reporting Throughout the process, technicians document their activities, findings, and © 489 any changes made during the maintenance task. This information is recorded for future reference, analysis, and compliance purposes. After completing the task, technicians prepare reports summarizing their work and any additional recommendations. Follow-up actions Depending on the findings during the maintenance task, further actions may be required. These actions can include ordering additional parts, scheduling follow-up visits, or updating preventive maintenance plans to prevent similar issues in the future. Closure and feedback Once the maintenance task is completed, the work order is closed, and relevant stakeholders are notified. Feedback from technicians, customers, or site representatives may be collected to assess the quality of the maintenance work and identify areas for improvement. Overall, plant maintenance activities are crucial for ensuring that technical systems remain operational and reliable. By conducting inspections, implementing preventive maintenance, carrying out repairs, and taking other necessary measures, your organization can keep its equipment functioning optimally and minimize downtimes. Plant maintenance seamlessly integrates with other components of the SAP ERP system, including materials management, quality management, production planning, sales and distribution, finance, controlling, and human resources. By integrating with other modules, such as materials management, production, sales and distribution, personnel management, and controlling, plant maintenance ensures that data is always up-to-date. This integration also triggers necessary processes in plant maintenance and customer service in other areas of the SAP ERP system. For example, when you need to purchase a non- stock material, a purchase requisition is automatically generated in the materials management/purchasing area. The integration of plant maintenance with other SAP ERP modules ensures that the data in each module remains up- to-date and can trigger processes in other functions as necessary. The cornerstone of plant maintenance is its master data, which is stored in and managed through centralized master data tables. Within plant maintenance, various types of master data exist, including equipment, functional locations, specifications for objects, characteristics, task lists, codes containing Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 490 maintenance history data, material bills of materials (BOMs), measuring points, and captured data about equipment use, such as wear and tear or consumption. This master data serves as the foundation for creating transactional data in SAP ERP. For instance, plant maintenance can use master data to create a maintenance record, material management can create a purchase order, production planning can create a production order, and sales and distribution can create a sales order. The integration of SAP EWM with plant maintenance through SAP Enterprise Asset Management (SAP EAM) enables you to easily use and adapt the system, resulting in a fast time-to-value and a low total cost of ownership (TCO). SAP EWM offers many advantages for streamlining warehouse operations, increasing productivity, and improving accuracy. Meanwhile, plant maintenance (in SAP EAM) automates the process of handling facility repair and maintenance requests for assets. Plant maintenance order-driven warehouse operations are crucial for ensuring the timely availability of spare parts and for reducing repair time. The primary goal of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM is to enhance efficiency, integration, and visibility throughout warehouse execution as well as reap the following benefits: Successful deployment of an improved integration package across multiple customer locations. Flexibility to incorporate customer-specific requirements from plant maintenance orders for integration and warehouse operations. Two integration approach options—the delivery-based option and the production material request (PMR)-based option—can be pursued, depending on the type of industry (i.e., mining, oil & gas, or manufacturing) and the complexity of the customer process. Leveraging SAP EWM’s standard warehouse process capability and functionalities for all core processes, including handheld radio frequency (RF) devices. Optimizing warehouse operations by utilizing consolidation and cross- docking based on plant maintenance orders. Process and industry expertise in plant maintenance orders and warehouse management. © 491 Figure 9.1 shows the two options for integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM. Figure 9.1 Plant Maintenance-SAP EWM Integration Let’s briefly discuss these two integration approaches: Delivery-based integration This option is primarily used for the maintenance of heavy engineering assets, such as in the mining and oil & gas industries. As shown in Figure 9.2, delivery-based integration for plant maintenance mainly covers following high-level processes: Creation and release of plant maintenance orders for pick parts in SAP S/4HANA Creation of an outbound delivery and its replication in SAP EWM Creation of waves for pick parts, based on the outbound delivery order in SAP EWM Picking, staging, and loading plant maintenance parts from warehouses in SAP EWM Performing goods issues in SAP EWM Updating material document and reservation data for the plant maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Figure 9.2 Delivery-Based Integration Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 492 PMR-based integration This option is primarily used for the maintenance of production assets in manufacturing plants, such as automotive and consumer goods. The PMR-based integration option is not available as an out-of-the-box SAP EWM solution. To use this functionality, an add-on from SAP Consulting is available for the integration with PMR. As shown in Figure 9.3, a plant maintenance order using PMR has several features including the following: A new object, called the production material request, offers greater flexibility in staging processes within SAP EWM. The new EWM staging option has been added to the control cycle in addition to the existing pick parts and release order part options. The system supports single-order staging, cross-order staging, and manual staging. Status and quantity updates for manufacturing orders are supported. The system allows for user-driven staging via desktop transactions or staging in the background. Figure 9.3 PMR-Based Integration © 493

sections.en: 9.2 Using Plant Maintenance Orders In this section, we’ll show you how to use plant maintenance for goods issues and goods receipts. We’ll begin with the outbound process and then cover the inbound process. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process, configuration, and master data setup needed and then provide a process demonstration.

sections.title: Outbound Process
sections.en: 9.2.1 Outbound Process In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the outbound goods issue process using plant maintenance orders with the delivery-based integration deployment option. This section is divided into four parts: business process, configuration required for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow. Business Process An outbound process in plant maintenance typically refers to activities involved in the maintenance and repair of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure outside of the plant or facility where they are located. This process involves coordinating and managing the necessary resources, personnel, and materials to execute maintenance tasks at external sites. The overall business process for a goods issue of a material to a maintenance order is shown in Figure 9.4. The key steps involved in an outbound process with plant maintenance include the following: 1. The outbound process typically starts in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when a maintenance order is created. The outbound delivery is created with reference to the maintenance order. The outbound delivery is created in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA but is automatically is replicated to SAP EWM for further processing. 2. In SAP EWM, a wave is created for the outbound delivery order. Upon wave release, a warehouse task to pick the material is automatically created. The pick warehouse task is based on the picking strategy for the plant maintenance material. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 494 Figure 9.4 Outbound Process Using Plant Maintenance Orders 3. The plant maintenance material is further picked, packed, and loaded as per the warehouse process. Once the process is completed, the warehouse team performs goods the issue for the outbound delivery order, and the outbound process is completed. 4. The plant maintenance team consumes the material, and the cost of the material is booked against the maintenance order. By following these steps, the outbound process in plant maintenance ensures effective management of maintenance tasks at external sites, enabling the timely resolution of equipment or system issues to maintain operational efficiency and reliability. Configuration In this section, we’ll cover the key customization options required for this process, assuming that the main SAP EWM customization settings have already been configured in the system: 1. Init. Com. field, and enter the SAP EWM document type in the Document Type field, as shown in Figure 9.7. Figure 9.7 Assignment of SAP ERP Document Type 4. sections.title: Inbound Process
sections.en: 9.2.2 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the inbound return goods receipt process by utilizing SAP S/4HANA, SAP EWM. This section is divided into four © 507 parts: inbound goods receipt business process, configuration needed for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow. Business Process The goods receipt process with plant maintenance involves receiving and recording goods or materials delivered to a plant or facility, as well as managing any associated maintenance activities. The maintenance return order process with SAP EWM typically involves several steps to ensure the smooth return of goods for maintenance or repair purposes. As shown in Figure 9.29, this process involves the following steps: 1. The process begins with the creation of a maintenance return order in SAP EWM. This order is generated to initiate the return process and includes relevant details such as the material, quantity, and reason for return as well as any specific instructions. 2. A maintenance order is changed in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to initiate the process of returning goods to the store. During the process of goods receipt, an inbound delivery will be created, which is then replicated to SAP EWM in the background. 3. When the material is physically received in the warehouse, the warehouse team generates a warehouse task and physically places the material in the storage area in the SAP EWM system. A putaway strategy is defined for plant maintenance materials, guiding warehouse operators to physically store the material in the designated area and confirm the warehouse task accordingly. 4. Upon arrival at the warehouse, the returned materials are received into the SAP EWM system. The goods receipt process involves capturing information such as the quantity received, inspection details (if applicable), and any discrepancies identified during the inspection 5. After the material is stored in the designated area, the warehouse team performs a goods receipt in SAP EWM, which generates inventory in both the SAP EWM and SAP S/4HANA systems 6. The plant maintenance team can now further book labor hours, and the maintenance order is technically complete. sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 9.3 Summary That’s it! You’re now prepared to begin setting up plant maintenance in your own organization. In this chapter, we provided an overview of plant maintenance, discussing both the delivery-based plant maintenance order process and PMR-based plant maintenance order process with SAP EWM. Furthermore, we explored the inbound goods receipt process and the outbound goods issue process using the integration between SAP EWM, plant maintenance, and either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com 520 10 SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals offers invaluable assistance to pharmaceutical companies in fulfilling their specific legal obligations regarding the serialization, tracking, and tracing of products as well as in diligently reporting compliance with pharmaceutical product regulations from the relevant regulatory bodies. Moreover, this solution facilitates seamless data exchanges with packaging lines and enhances collaboration with supply chain partners, such as warehouse operations, third-party logistics (3PL), and contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs). SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals seamlessly integrates with diverse business processes, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, transactions, warehouse management, and supply chain management, thereby streamlining operations comprehensively. By placing paramount emphasis on patient safety, SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals helps protect company reputations. Furthermore, the meticulous management of serial numbers presents a formidable challenge for counterfeiters attempting to replicate legitimate codes, thereby serving as a deterrent against fraud. The primary aim of this chapter is to provide comprehensive information regarding SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals. SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals can be seamlessly integrated to deliver complete end- to-end visibility and control over the storage and movement of pharmaceutical products within warehouses and distribution centers. In typical business scenarios, whenever a serialized item is moved in or out of a warehouse, it is imperative to update both the stock management and the serialization repository accordingly. However, updating these two separate systems separately poses a significant risk of data inconsistency. The Warehouse integration feature addresses this issue by enabling the integration of warehouse stock with the serialization repository, ensuring data consistency and minimizing the risk of errors. This integration feature facilitates the © 521 synchronization of data between the SAP EWM and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals systems, enabling real-time updates of stock movements and serialization data. This ensures that all information related to the pharmaceutical products is captured and maintained accurately, enabling efficient tracking and tracing of the product at every stage of the supply chain. Overall, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals is a powerful solution that enables seamless data synchronization and data consistency, providing complete visibility and control over pharmaceutical products within a warehouse or distribution center. The introductory section of this chapter is an overview of SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals and highlights how the solution can facilitate growth. The chapter then focuses on the diverse options available for Inbound goods receipt process and Outbound goods issue with business process, configuration, master data and end to end demonstration of process. The chapter will particularly emphasize the SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals solution, an SAP system specifically designed for the efficient management of serial numbers and repositories. The central focus of this chapter will revolve around the integration of SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals with SAP EWM for handling the inbound goods receipt process. Finally, we’ll focus on the integration of SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals with SAP EWM, a powerful warehouse management system (WMS) offered by SAP. This integration plays a pivotal role in facilitating the smooth and efficient handling of the inbound goods receipt process. By the end of this chapter, you’ll possess a comprehensive understanding of SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals, its integration with SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals solution, and its seamless incorporation with SAP EWM for inbound and outbound process This knowledge will equip you with valuable insights into the advanced technologies employed in the pharmaceutical industry, ensuring you’re well-informed and prepared to tackle related challenges effectively.
